#134230. Your Guide to Running on the Treadmill This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2297 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Your Guide to Running on the Treadmill This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2297 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there’s almost no other cardio machine that brings up as many feelings as the treadmill.
  • Industry observers note that then, last winter happened.
  • According to recent reports, but, as any treadmill hater knows, moving a run indoors isn’t as simple as it sounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there’s almost no other cardio machine that brings up as many feelings as the treadmill. For the first few years of my running career, I’d do just about everything I could to avoid hopping on one, even if that meant running in freezing temps or heavy rain.

Industry observers note that then, last winter happened. There was more snow and ice on the ground in New York City than I had seen in a long time, but I had a half-marathon to train for. It left me no choice: I had to move my workouts to the treadmill unless I wanted to end up like that meme where the woman notes snow is the perfect texture for running just to wipe out on live television a few seconds later.

According to recent reports, but, as any treadmill hater knows, moving a run indoors isn’t as simple as it sounds. A lot changes on a tread—form, mental stimulation, pace—and it can totally mess with your head. Once you understand why, though, it’s a lot easier to work with the treadmill instead of against it; here’s how.

Because it is! For starters, your form changes. “Many people shorten their stride on the treadmill—me included,” states Amy Woods, a USAT-certified run coach and ISSA-certified strength and conditioning coach. “We also tend to run a little more upright.”.

Industry observers note that there’s a simple reason behind it. When you’re running outside, your legs have all the space they need for each stride, but on a treadmill, you’re contained to the length and width of the belt. Plus, most people tend to stick too close to the front of the tread, making their space even smaller, notes Morgan Mowers, PT, DPT, a physical therapist and V.02-certified run coach.

Sources indicate that between a shortened stride and the fact that it’s a bit easier to propel yourself forward when you’ve got the help of the moving belt, you end up using different muscles on a treadmill compared to outdoors. “We see a decrease in activation of hamstrings and glutes, those bigger propellers that push you forward,” Mowers says. Instead, you’re seeing more activation in your hip flexors, quads, calves, and knees.

Sources indicate that on paper, a lot of these differences should actually make treadmill running easier than running outside. Another example? A treadmill provides a consistent surface. Outside, terrain and incline can vary with each step, so you call on more stabilizing muscles in your ankles and calves, Mowers claims. “With every step, there's a little bit of a change when you're running outside versus on a treadmill,” she says. “Even if you are changing up the incline, it's the same exact surface over and over again.” You also don’t have to deal with the same environmental challenges—like heat and wind resistance—that come with running outside. There’s even a famous 1996 study that claims runners should set their incline to 1 percent to accommodate for the difference.

Even with all these easier-sounding differences, running on a treadmill often feels anything but. For many people, myself included, slowing down on a treadmill is the norm. One possible reason: You may just not be used to it, Woods says. Running safely on a treadmill, especially at higher speeds, takes practice. “It's definitely a different feeling when you're running on a treadmill,” Woods says. “You have to be more aware of your foot placement, your arm swing, and where your eyes are looking.” Even if you’re not consciously aware of it, your proprioception (your ability to sense your body’s position in space) could be affected.

Industry observers note that plus, when you’re on the treadmill, you’re stuck at one pace unless you change it, Mowers points out. “That consistency that your body is feeling on a treadmill can make it feel harder, and also may result in you going at an overall slower pace,” she says. When you hop on a treadmill, you start yourself at a pace and settle in until you physically change it. Over the course of a mile outdoors, in comparison, you may start at an 11:00 pace, then speed up to a 10:45 pace for most of it, and end up cruising at a 10:30 pace—all without really noticing. Even though your effort feels the same, your outdoor mile ends up faster.

Then there’s the mental side of things. Outside, you’ve got much more stimulation, says Rachelle Reed, PhD, an exercise physiologist. Your surroundings can offer the perfect distraction, and the natural variations in scenery, incline, terrain, and pace can help keep your brain more engaged too. This can have an impact on your rate of perceived exertion (RPE), Reed says. In fact, a 2019 meta-analysis found that at faster speeds, runners rated their effort as harder on a treadmill compared to outdoors. Basically, it’s harder to go hard on the tread. And because running on a treadmill is technically easier than running outdoors because you have less variation, wind resistance, and environmental factors to navigate at any given moment, that higher RPE really speaks to the mental effects of being inside, Reed says.

It has been revealed that the good news? All these differences between treadmill and outdoor running only really matter if you’re training for a race. That’s because come race day, you’ll want your muscles fully prepped to accommodate your outdoor stride, along with the ability to run across inconsistent terrain and in various elements, Mowers claims. Meanwhile, if you’re just looking to do cardio, you can take your pick between the two.

In a recent development, if you are in fact training for a race, how should a treadmill fit into your training? In this case, going outside tends to be superior to staying in, our experts agree. Don’t move your run to the tread at just any sign of inconvenience—running in the rain, cold, and (reasonable) heat all make you a better runner, and you never know if those conditions will pop up on race day, so you’ll be glad to have the practice.

Still, there are definitely situations where it’s not a good idea to go outside. Mowers draws the line when it comes to safety: If the ground is icy, snowy, or slippery in any way, she’ll stay inside to avoid potential injury. If temps are dangerously hot, she’ll run on the treadmill. If there’s risk from serious weather, like thunder and lightning or flooding, she’ll also stay safe indoors. And, she’ll stick to her tread in the event of poor air quality (anything that’s an air quality index over 101).

Recent findings suggest that it’s always worth considering personal safety, too. If your only window to run is late at night and you feel more comfortable staying indoors, do that.

How hot is too hot? This is going to vary down to the person and place. Anything above 85 degrees can be dangerous, Woods states, and you also need to factor in dew point, humidity, and the effort of your run. (Harder efforts are more risky than easier ones.) If temps are higher and you decide to run outdoors, make sure you bring plenty of hydration and fuel, go slower than normal, and pay attention to signs of overheating.

According to recent reports, there’s also the convenience factor. You may need to do a run on the treadmill because it’s more accommodating to your schedule or childcare needs. That’s totally okay too. Ideally, the majority of your runs (we’re talking about 80 percent, and especially your long runs) will be outside, but if you’re someone who finds themselves needing to do the bulk of their running indoors, a run coach can help you make sure you’re prepped for race day. (Woods works with athletes who do the bulk of their training on treads—it’s possible!) The treadmill exists for a reason, and your training will not be affected by the occasional indoor run.

Sources indicate that first and foremost, don’t be too hard on yourself about pace. “I always disconnect from pace on the treadmill,” Woods says. Instead, she focuses on her time and RPE. It’s really about thinking about the “spirit of the workout,” she says. For example, you can pay attention to what heart rate zone or effort level you’re supposed to get to and match that—even if that looks slower and feels harder indoors.

Recent findings suggest that and, no, you don’t need to set your incline to 1 percent to compensate for bringing your workout indoors, our experts agree. The biggest reason? The study that established the idea was very small (it had just nine participants) and done only in men. That mentioned, the incline buttons will become useful depending on the kind of run you have on deck for the day.

Industry observers note that finally, give yourself a good warm-up on the treadmill, Mowers states. “Just the act of getting on a treadmill is going to increase our heart rate a little bit because we're a hamster on a wheel; we're trying not to fall off of this thing, and we're so aware of the fact that we're running,” she says. You may need at least 10 to 15 minutes to settle in before getting started with the rest of your workout.

Here’s how to approach different kinds of runs indoors.

Nothing really has to change, Woods notes. It may take you a little longer to run a 5K on your treadmill, but try to stick to the appropriate lower heart rate zones and RPE that you’d normally achieve on these kinds of runs outdoors.

Recent findings suggest that you can play with incline if you’d like—but it’s not a requirement if this is a one-off run you’re doing inside. Running for one day on a completely flat surface won’t affect your training. One reason you may want to try changing the incline may simply be because it adds some variety and stimulation, Woods says. If you’re someone who struggles because the treadmill feels boring, try increasing the incline anywhere from 1 to 4 percent for anywhere from 30 seconds to a few minutes every so often.

Another hack: Every 10 minutes, increase your speed slightly. That should give you enough time to warm up a little each time and settle into the pace, so you shouldn’t see much of a jump in demand on your heart rate or effort.

This one gets a bit trickier, Woods notes. Going at all-out speeds on a treadmill can be much tougher—and not feel super safe. This is a time when you’ll want to think about the spirit of the workout. If you have intervals where you’re supposed to get to max heart rate efforts, instead of turning up the speed super high, you can increase the incline in addition to adjusting the speed slightly, Woods says. That should still get you to your zone 4 or 5, all while allowing you to stay slower and feel more in control. This is much easier to accomplish in a tempo run (where you’re holding the pace for longer chunks of time) compared to intervals, so you could also swap an interval run for tempo too.

According to recent reports, you also have the option to skip a speed workout, Woods says. Missing one session won’t have an impact on your training, and if you’d rather not do it on the treadmill, you also have the option to switch it with another run for the week.

It has been revealed that now, here’s a workout that translates pretty well to the treadmill: All you have to do is up your incline for the duration marked in your workout. Woods recommends sticking between 1 and 4 percent as a good rule of thumb, but you can always bump up to 5 to 8 as long as you can keep good run form.

Recent findings suggest that ideally, you can move your long run to another day when you can run outside. But, if not, go by time—not mileage. Woods doesn’t recommend running on a treadmill for longer than two hours unless you are very experienced on one because of how it affects your form.

You also have the option to break up your run and do 90 minutes in the morning and 90 minutes in the afternoon. “This will help with form deterioration which is more noticeable and can be more dangerous on a tread,” Woods says.

It has been revealed that while you’re on your long run, you’ll also want to incorporate moments of incline running and even some pace variation—both for improving your running and also giving yourself a mental reset. Woods also loves to sprinkle in 15- to 30-second walking breaks every mile or so to reset her form and hydrate.

Recent findings suggest that then the world is really your oyster on the treadmill, but all the same ideas apply: Focus on time and effort, not pace. And, feel free to sprinkle in different inclines and speeds to work different heart rate zones and find moments of mental reset.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) kept leaving crypto exchanges this week as the price of the meme cryptocurrency fell to levels last seen in the spring of 2021, and on Wednesday, the outflow picked up sharply.

According to CoinGlass data, 520.83 billion SHIB left exchanges over the past 24 hours. That amount made up most of the 757.51 billion SHIB that exchanges lost over the past seven days, and over the past 30 days, the outflow reached 2.88 trillion SHIB.

On Wednesday evening, SHIB was trading at $0.00000344, according to CoinGlass. So far this week, the token was down 4.78%, and its market capitalization went down to $2.02 billion, according to TradingView.

According to recent reports, according to the weekly chart on TradingView, SHIB last traded at these levels in the spring of 2021, months before the token reached its all-time high of $0.00008845 on Oct. 28, 2021.

From early 2026 until mid-November, the price of SHIB held above $0.000004, and the yearly low stood at $0.00000411 at the July 17 close. In November, SHIB fell to $0.00000373, and in late November, the token dropped as low as $0.00000337. On Jan. 1, the token closed the day at $0.00000692, and since the start of the year, SHIB has lost 50.3% of its value, according to CoinGlass. As of Nov. 22, SHIB had lost 22.7% in November so far, according to CryptoRank.

The latest drop in SHIB came after Bitcoin fell back below $60,000 this week. On Saturday, Nov. 21, Bitcoin dropped as low as $55,150, its lowest price since September 2024. Over the past 24 hours, $57,590 worth of SHIB futures positions were liquidated, and $54,750 of that amount came from long positions on OKX, according to CoinGlass.

Recent findings suggest that the Wednesday outflow was not the first large one this month. On Nov. 17, about 312 billion SHIB were withdrawn from exchanges, according to CryptoQuant. On the same day, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million, according to Etherscan.

Recent findings suggest that coinGlass data also shows that since late 2024, the total SHIB balance on exchanges has gone down by 19.18 trillion tokens, or 20.54%, to 74.19 trillion, and over the same period, the price of SHIB fell by 88.39%. The remaining 74.19 trillion SHIB on exchanges make up 12.59% of the circulating supply and are worth about $254.75 million.

Most of the 24-hour outflow came from exchanges that CoinGlass groups as "Others," as their combined SHIB balance fell by 88.5% to 70.93 billion tokens. Over the same period, the SHIB balances of Binance and OKX barely changed, and Coinbase, Bitfinex and Bitstamp added SHIB.

As a result, in the week when the price of SHIB fell to levels last seen in 2021, exchanges lost more SHIB in a single day than over the previous six days combined, according to CoinGlass data.

Industry observers note that businesses can make their own stablecoins on Cardano [ADA] now! Could this be what the platform’s DeFi scene has been waiting for?

The Cardano Foundation is in the news today after confirming the launch on X.

Businesses on Cardano can now do one of two things. They can create a stablecoin under their own brand, or use stablecoins Brale already supports.

Companies can also swap dollars for stablecoins, cash back out to fiat, and send transfers.

The service reaches 30 blockchains.

It’s powered by CIP-113, which lets issuers attach rules to their tokens. A organization could allow transfers only between approved wallets, or keep the power to freeze tokens if needed. It’s handy for regulated businesses, and it also means apps need to check each token’s rules before working with it.

Here’s what’s sticky though. The Foundation hasn’t mentioned which businesses are issuing tokens at launch. It also didn’t share any figures on expected issuance or payment volume.

For all the hype, ADA’s turned a blind eye to all that.

At press time, the altcoin was valued at $0.138 following a 5% dip in 24 hours. A month ago, it was near $0.21. Most of the damage came later, including the major fall on the 14th.

According to recent reports, on 23rd November, the RSI went up to 32 and the MACD line climbed above the Signal line. It looked like sellers were losing grip for a while, but that didn’t last long. In fact, the RSI has since fallen back to 27, below its own average, and into oversold territory again.

Simply put, ADA may be cheap, but it looks like buyers can’t be plied right now.

It has been revealed that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

It has been revealed that IN A WORLD where home workout trends change with the seasons, the exercise bike continues to stand the test of time. Its appeal lies in its ability to increase cardiovascular health through a low-impact approach, with limitless ability to take it up a notch. With a range of indoor exercise bike styles available, from air bikes to spin bikes and even recumbent bikes, it can be difficult to choose the right style for your fitness goals and preferences.

Recent innovations in "smart" bikes have expanded the indoor bike market even further, offering a wider selection than ever before. So we leveraged the extensive collective experience of MH fitness editors, anchored by months of hands-on testing from certified trainers, to distinguish which factors set the top options apart from the rest.

Each of the bikes in this guide can help consumers burn calories and improve overall fitness, but certain styles diverge in fundamental ways. Spin bikes, similar to what you might find at a SoulCycle class, engage your core and legs, while air bikes require you to use your upper body as well. Air bike enthusiasts appreciate their effectiveness in high-intensity interval training and circuit-style workouts due to their ability to require quick bursts of intense effort. Meanwhile, spin bikes cater to a broader range of intensities, longer cycling sessions, and supplementing outdoor cycling routines.

Sources indicate that to help you select the ideal exercise bike for you and your home gym, we've curated a list of the top exercise bikes we've personally tested, fitting all budget levels. From the ultra-high-end Peloton Bike+ to the most budget-friendly options available on Amazon, we've got you covered. Continue scrolling to discover the seven best exercise bikes, according to fitness editors and certified trainers, but first, a few things to keep in mind.

Being the Fitness and Reviews Editor of Men's Health means I get my hands on every piece of new gym gear that releases, sometimes before it's available to the public. To build this guide of the best exercise bikes, I took stock of the bestselling bikes on the market and put them up against overlooked classics and newly released options. I used each of these bikes for months, during long rides, interval training, as a warm-up, or a workout finisher.

Sources indicate that over the years, Men's Health editors like fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, CSCS, as well as key fitness trainers from both the MH Advisory Board and the MH Strength in Diversity Initiative, have taken great care in researching and evaluating the wide pool of exercise bikes. Their insights were also integral in creating this list. Our team also enlisted the help of Maillard Howell of Dean CrossFit in Brooklyn to test and assess how well these bikes performed in a real-world scenario (read: a high-volume, high-traffic training facility).

Ultimately, we ended up with the below guide that represents our top picks for the best exercise bikes we recommend buying now.

Sources indicate that this new REP Fitness bike is one of the most impressive air bikes that our Fitness Director, Ebenezer Samuel, CSCS, has ever used. “The eight damper settings create a ton of options for my training,” he notes. “And they essentially let the Strive simulate just about any air bike on the market.”.

Industry observers note that this Variable Pitch Resistance (VPR) system allows you to change the angle of the fan blades to give you that additional control over your workout. Most of us recognize the air bike for its impressive ability to make you suffer more the harder that you pedal it.

But with this new system, the Strive bike gives you the ability to use it for steady-state and recovery rides as well as those brutal finisher and max-effort sessions.

“At an 8, this feels like a serious strength-style quad-pump that's harder per pedal than a Rogue Echo or Scwhinn Airdyne,” says Samuel. “That versatility, and the speed with which you can switch between settings, opens a upcoming world of fan bike workouts.”.

The Strive is also as sturdy as they come among fanbikes. Underrated: The cupholder is everything you want on a bike, suitable for small plastic bottles and larger metal jugs alike (and great for your iPhone too).

In a recent development, this bike is no slouch when it comes to its hardware. In fact, it offers many of the same features as bikes double its price. From adjustable handlebars to convenient dumbbell holders, 32 levels of resistance, toe-cage pedals, and a spacious touchscreen display, it boasts all the features you'd expect from a premium bike. And it's wrapped in a sleek, matte black finish that oozes style.

Industry observers note that the assembly is fairly easy, taking about 45 minutes to set up. The bike arrives in a box about 85 percent built with just the feet, handles, and pedals needing to be mounted. The bike has a nice compact frame and takes up the least amount of space in the home. The brand found a way to cut down on the cost by removing the expensive touchscreen and giving you a platform to place your own mobile device or tablet on, allowing you to follow any classes you want that way.

Whether we were sprinting or climbing out of the saddle during intense workouts, this bike offered unwavering stability. We never found ourselves wobbling or feeling uneasy on this machine. The elevated bullhorn handlebars aren’t just about style; they provide an elbow rest that we found essential during grueling climbs. It's a thoughtful touch that we found enhances overall riding comfort. The competition-style seat on this bike strikes a balance between comfort and support that other bikes we've tested in this price range miss the mark on. It's designed for long sessions, providing that Goldilocks level of cushioning.

This bike offers an all-around fantastic workout experience, especially for the cost, and is a great pick no matter your goals.

The NordicTrack X24 earned its spot here because it doesn't just deliver cutting-edge training technology to the user, it also delivers the world for those more adventure-minded riders.

Do you want to feel like you are cycling through the Swiss Alps or along the beaches of Hawaii? That's what the NordicTrack offers, and not just by showing pretty landscapes on its 22-inch screen. Unlike the other bikes in this guide that simulate incline and decline by adjusting the magnetic resistance, this one actually replicates climbs or descents for a more accurate feeling of winding up and down the hills of Switzerland.

Industry observers note that the setup is easy enough to do solo, but it helps if you have a person around to help you for some of the more involved moments of assembly. The bike is sturdy and robust, but also heavy, weighing over 200 pounds. So be sure that you build it in close proximity to where you are going to want to ride it, because it's not very easy to move around.

Like most NordicTrack equipment, the X24 comes with a year-long iFit membership.

Industry observers note that looking for a bike that can handle years of punishment? Well, if the end of the world comes knocking, the Rogue Echo Bike will likely still be pedaling away. This thing is solid as a rock, capable of handling whatever you throw its way. This bike is a strength builder and a monster maker, demanding legit power from the user to make it move.

It has been revealed that the bike arrives at your door well-packaged and about 80 percent assembled. The screen, arms, pedals, and feet are all that you need to mount. The process can take about an hour to get your bike ready to ride.

Its belt drive system is consistent and essentially maintenance-free, meaning you can focus on your workout, not tinkering around with the machine. We've used this bike on and off for more than seven years and have never experienced technical complications.

Industry observers note that beyond its durability, this bike rides like a dream. Pedaling is smooth and fluid in motion, and returns more resistance in response to the rider's effort.

We don't just recommend this bike; we swear by it. Years of firsthand testing have made it abundantly clear that if air bikes had Oscars, this one would be walking away with the golden statue, no doubt.Another unique feature of the Rogue Echo Bike is its fan blades. They’re crafted from thin-gauge steel, cut out and treated to a powder coating and welded to a central hub within the fan cage. While this level of detail might seem unnecessary, it adds to the fan's long-term reliability and overall aesthetic.

Industry observers note that now, we won't sugarcoat it; this machine is heavy. But fear not, because it comes equipped with wheels at the front. So, even if you're not the Hulk, you can still shuffle it around to ensure it fits in your workout space.

The only other qualm we have with this bike is that it doesn't feature multi-grip handles like other air bike models do.

Sources indicate that there's a reason that Peloton's bikes have remained popular through the highs and lows of at-home training. The brand combines a superbly designed, connected bike with a charismatic crew of trainers and has ignited a fitness following.

In a recent development, the delivery is taken care of by Peloton, which unboxes and mounts the bike for you at your chosen location—an example of the high level of service that comes from the brand. The bike itself is fairly durable, and relatively simplistic outside of the 21.5-inch HD touchscreen. If you are interested in also utilizing the strength classes, consider Peloton's Cross Training Bike+, which comes with a pair of dumbbells and additional amenities like built-in Sonos speakers.

The truth is, when you buy a Peloton you are buying more than a bike, you are buying a community. And you are getting a best-in-class library of instructor-led, studio-style classes. From cycling to off-bike sessions like core workouts and hybrid strength classes, the variety of content is endless. The engaging live class offerings and fun gamification of your data makes the bike especially great for beginners or anyone who has difficulty maintaining a regimen.

It has been revealed that on the downside, the initial investment can be a detractor, and the monthly subscription fee for access to Peloton's classes can also add up ($49.99 a month for all-access). However, if you fully utilize the platform and its library of classes, it can be a worthwhile expense.

In a recent development, the only other matter that our team had was instead of a traditional foot cage, the Peloton requires Delta-compatible cleats (which you can buy here) that clip into the pedals. It’s another step, and another purchase, before you start your ride. But this is to allow for the best experience with the programmed classes and resistance level changes, so it's an understandable ask. Peloton also offers a 30-day in-home trial with free delivery, setup, and, if needed, pickup and return for a small fee of $150. It's a commitment to customer satisfaction that helps protect your investment in this bike.

In a recent development, what we like about the Schwinn Fitness 290 Recumbent Bike is its excellent value. Sure, it doesn't have an overly huge touchscreen display, but that means you aren't tricked into spending your money on a bunch of technology you don't need. Plus, you can place your phone, tablet, or other device on the media shelf so you can ride along to on-demand, trainer-led classes with real-time coaching.

Industry observers note that the seat's padding provides a lot of cushioning and ventilation, meaning you won't want to cut your workout short because you're uncomfortable. The weighted strapped pedals are also a win, because they feel secure on your feet so you can focus on your ride and not whether you’re going to lose traction.

The relatively lightweight build of this bike is also a positive, as anyone who has shopped for a recumbent bike understands. The majority of models are built like tanks, making them very hard to move around the house. The 290 also comes with rollers, making it even easier to transport.

Recent findings suggest that how well this is built should be no surprise considering how long Schwinn has been in the bike game. This model is extremely comfortable for most sizes, including taller individuals, which is a nice improvement from the previous 230 version.

Read More: The Best Recumbent Bikes, Tested by Us.

We understand that some of the bikes in this guide might be a little expensive for beginners who aren’t certain if they can stick with a latest cardio routine or don’t need something that can handle intense workouts.

Merach is a brand that we’ve tested decent products from, and other pieces of its equipment have made our guides in the past. This design won’t take up much space, and it offers a good range of intensity through magnetic resistance.

Industry observers note that now, if you’re looking for an exercise bike that is going to take a lot of punishment and will handle whatever you throw at it, you might want to consider one of the more serious models above. This ride is only 62 pounds, which absolutely puts it on the lighter side and therefore prone to a little less stability if you’re really jamming on it.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for an easy-to-use bike from a trusted manufacturer, this is your best play for the money. And owners on Amazon have commented on how quiet it is, with Merach putting it under 25 decibels in use.

It has been revealed that in general, both devices can work for both high-intensity interval training workouts and long cardio. But how you prioritize your training will determine which bike is best for you. If you blueprint to focus on HIIT-based workouts, or want to mix weight training and bodyweight in with your bike work, the air bike is your jam. It’s easier to dismount the bike after a one-minute interval, then do a set of pushups, for example, making this ideal if you love CrossFit-style training.

If those steady-state workouts are your focus or you're using an indoor exercise bike to supplement outdoor riding, hop on a spin bike and get ready to pedal. And if you like doing cardio while watching TV, also opt for the spin bike; fan bikes are incredibly loud.

According to recent reports, everyone has different fitness levels and goals, but not every bike can cater to these needs. Look for a bike with adjustable resistance levels, allowing you to customize the intensity of your workouts however you choose. This is especially important if you're planning to evolve the intensity of your workouts in the coming months and years.

In a recent development, magnetic resistance is often the smoothest, most predictable option, which is what you can find in most spin bikes. This allows bike makers like Peloton to seamlessly integrate the resistance level with its online classes. While air bike options like Rogue and Assault use traditional methods of wheel fans and friction to challenge your endurance.

The display should be easy to use and show all the essentials, including speed, distance, and time. Extra features like a heart rate monitor, Bluetooth connectivity, and USB ports can be nice to have, so decide if any of those are dealbreakers for you. For the higher-end spin bikes, the screens are more like full-service entertainment centers that can be used to watch a class with your favorite trainer or take you through a great cycling route in the Alps.

Some exercise bikes include preset workout programs, while others may offer a membership-based training app. Consider if having built-in programs is notable to you, and if it is, if you want to consider a membership that would allow for a greater library of programs. There is typically a cost involved, so if you plan on using those features, be sure to confirm whether or not they are included. In some cases, these bikes might work perfectly without those higher-level subscriptions.

Consider the dimensions of the bikes you're shopping for, especially if you have limited space. Some bikes come with compact designs and foldable options for easier storage. If you'll need to stow the bike away when not in use, look for a lightweight frame on wheels.

In a recent development, because exercise bikes are such a significant investment, budget and warranty go hand-in-hand. Many of the bike models we recommend offer a solid warranty of between one and seven years on parts, plus at least a one-year warranty on labor. This is totally reasonable, especially if you're spending north of $1,500 on a new machine. You should expect that your bike's frame and resistance mechanism should both be warrantied for the life of the unit.

It has been revealed that A 2019 study showed that regular use of an exercise bike—alone or combined with strength training—can have a positive impact on aerobic capacity in as little as three months. Researchers also concluded that, like other forms of regular cardio, using an exercise bike can also contribute to a reduction in systolic and diastolic blood pressure—especially when combined with a heart-healthy diet.

Indoor cycling is also a low-impact form of cardio, resulting in less pressure on the joints than activities like running or jumping. Cycling is not a load-bearing exercise, says Kate Heelan, PhD, a Professor of Research at the University of Nebraska at Kearney. This helps to minimize the risk of injury caused by malalignment, loss of balance, etc.

According to recent reports, it's hard to beat the fresh air and sense of freedom an outdoor ride offers, but indoor cycling has a few unique benefits that can't be duplicated on the road. It starts with the fact you can hit hills or flat road when and how you want, just with the press of a button.

Because you'll never quite be 'coasting' or riding downhill on an exercise bike, indoor cycling workouts can allow you to get the benefit of several hours’ worth of outdoor riding done in half the time.

Cycling is an amazing way to get in shape and stay healthy, there's no doubt about it. But when it comes to choosing between indoor and outdoor cycling, what are the real differences?

"Broadly, both devices will burn calories and offer cardiovascular benefit," says MH fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, CSCS, "But they’re not the same experience.".

Sources indicate that for starters, there's the convenience factor. Indoor cycling is ideal for those who are short on time or live in regions where the terrain or weather may limit getting a ride outdoors. It can be much easier to hop on an indoor bike at home or at the gym and get a great workout without having to worry about traffic, the environment, or safety concerns.

Recent findings suggest that both modalities lead to cardiovascular benefits and, like any activity, they both burn calories. But outdoor cycling challenges other qualities, claims Samuel. "You’re actively moving through space when you cycle outdoors," says Samuel, "which challenges your muscles to decelerate, react, and constantly micro-correct in ways it won’t on a stationary bike." The outdoor bike also offers a basic balance challenge that the indoor bike lacks.

Outdoors, the terrain and your pace set the challenge. Indoors, however, you can more easily customize your intensity, simply adjusting the resistance level on your bike. This (and the removal of the balance challenge) can make indoor cycling more beginner-friendly.

In a recent development, many indoor bikes offer an interactive component now, like instructor-led classes and competitive leaderboards, which can be a great way to stay motivated and challenge yourself. These classes also provide a sense of community and support to stay motivated and hungry, even when you're working out alone.

  • NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.
  • The Newly introduced York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role.

NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.

The Newly introduced York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.

Her distinction: settling share ownership and moving money across currencies are separate jobs, and winning one does not automatically secure the other.

According to Dr. Stevenson, Ava Labs unveiled that Avalanche would provide the core ledger for the clearing firm behind the proposed platform.

She cites Wall Street Journal reporting that Avalanche would be its sole settlement blockchain, with regulatory approval still required.

In a recent development, the proposed venue would support around-the-clock trading and near-instant settlement. Stevenson says NYSE tested Avalanche for roughly a year, prioritizing transaction speed, predictable costs and control over who can participate.

That permissioning capability matters for a regulated exchange. Avalanche (AVAX) can support customized networks with participation restrictions, rather than requiring the exchange to conduct settlement on an unrestricted public network.

AVAX rose as much as roughly 10% on the news, according to the video. Stevenson, who discloses holding the token, calls the selection a win for Avalanche, but cautions against treating infrastructure adoption as proof of investment returns.

“A network being used by a big name and its token being needed” are different things, she says. The announcement, in her account, provided neither revenue figures nor a commitment that NYSE would buy or hold AVAX.

Dr. Stevenson’s XRP thesis centers on overseas investors funding dollar-denominated stock purchases outside conventional banking hours.

A trader holding yen or another currency would need access to dollars or dollar-linked funding before buying U.S. shares.

She argues that this creates an opportunity for cross-border payment infrastructure, including XRP. But it remains a proposed use case, not a disclosed partnership: “I’m not telling you that NYSE is going to pick XRP for that.”.

Industry observers note that the YouTube video episode does not establish that XRP would be necessary for such funding. Nor does expanded trading access, by itself, demonstrate future demand for the token.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson also says the platform would support tokenized stocks issued across multiple blockchains, distinguishing asset issuance from the ledger used for settlement.

Those details matter more than a simple Avalanche-versus-XRP contest: the unresolved questions are which services institutions actually adopt, what generates revenue, and whether that activity requires either token.

#134222. Bitcoin ETFs shed $4 billion — How did one fund hide the cracks before leading the exit?

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2020 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ambcrypto ↗ Open Full Page

Bitcoin ETFs shed $4 billion — How did one fund hide the cracks before leading the exit?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2020 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $4.14 billion over three weeks, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly 84% of the withdrawals.
  • Sources indicate that in the week leading up to October 19, U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs appeared to be doing rather well.
  • It has been revealed that there was one small complication, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $4.14 billion over three weeks, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for roughly 84% of the withdrawals. However, the same fund had been concealing weakness elsewhere just weeks ago. The story behind the numbers is considerably more complicated than the headline.

Sources indicate that in the week leading up to October 19, U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs appeared to be doing rather well. The funds collectively attracted $301.2 million in net inflows. That’s quite a reassuring development for a market that had become accustomed to treating ETF demand as a barometer of Bitcoin’s institutional appeal.

It has been revealed that there was one small complication, though. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) had brought in $565.7 million on its own. Every other fund combined lost $264.5 million. So, how healthy was that $301.2 million gain if it depended entirely on one fund?

Three weeks later, the answer became harder to ignore.

Sources indicate that between November 2 and 20, Bitcoin ETFs suffered a staggering $4.14 billion in net withdrawals, according to Farside Investors. By the way, IBIT ALONE accounted for approximately $3.49 billion, or 84% of the exodus.

According to recent reports, and the selling gathered pace as the week wore on. Nearly $1.79 billion left in the final week, around 1.7 times the previous week’s withdrawals. From November 17 through November 20, each trading session ended with a larger outflow than the previous one.

October’s biggest source of support had become November’s biggest source of pressure. The reversal was striking enough. In fact, what was happening beneath it was more revealing!

BlackRock’s influence on the industry’s performance was hardly a one-week curiosity.

The pattern continued into October 26–30. IBIT attracted another $176.9 million while competing funds collectively lost $379.3 million. Even though the industry finished that week in the red, BlackRock’s inflows effectively absorbed nearly half the damage.

Then, on October 30, the reprieve ended.

Spot BTC ETFs recorded roughly $643 million in withdrawals in a single session, with IBIT contributing approximately $234 million. The fund that had been cushioning the industry’s losses was now participating in them.

November made that reversal unmistakable.

It has been revealed that IBIT accounted for approximately 94% of the industry’s net outflows during the first week, 85% during the second, and 76% during the third. Curiously, its share declined even as the third week brought the industry’s biggest outflow yet.

According to recent reports, that was the more consequential development. Other funds, including Fidelity’s FBTC and products from Grayscale and ARK, were contributing increasingly to the selling. What had initially been concentrated overwhelmingly in BlackRock’s product was beginning to spread.

A market once held up by its largest fund was now being dragged down by it, with competitors increasingly joining the retreat.

Now, IBIT was already by far the industry’s biggest fund. Perhaps its dominance in the withdrawals was simply a consequence of its size. Hence why that possibility deserved a closer look. However, a closer look at this position revealed another complication.

A fund holding most of the industry’s assets will naturally account for a significant share of its movements. A billion dollars leaving a $60 billion product is hardly equivalent to the same amount leaving one worth $5 billion.

By October 30, IBIT held approximately $62.7 billion in Bitcoin, according to iShares holdings data. Looking at it broadly, the Bitcoin ETF market held roughly $98.14 billion, based on SoSoValue.

It has been revealed that blackRock therefore controlled about two-thirds of the industry’s assets entering November. And yet, it accounted for 84% of the subsequent three-week net withdrawals.

The disparity only becomes sharper when adjusted for size.

Sources indicate that IBIT’s $3.49 billion outflow was equivalent to approximately 5.6% of its starting holdings value. For all the other funds combined, the equivalent was just 1.8%.

Industry observers note that in relative terms, BlackRock’s fund experienced roughly three times the withdrawal pressure of its competitors. Its scale explained part of its dominance, but hardly all of it.

Industry observers note that the underlying Bitcoin inventory tells a similar story. IBIT held approximately 811,817 BTC on October 30. By November 20, that had fallen to roughly 760,926 BTC, a reduction of nearly 50,900 BTC or 6.3%.

Sources indicate that bitcoin’s declining price could reduce the dollar value of those holdings, but it could not account for the disappearance of the coins themselves. IBIT’s inventory had genuinely contracted.

Industry observers note that the departures were measurable. The identities of those departing were another matter.

According to recent reports, A $4 billion ETF outflow makes it tempting to declare that institutional investors are abandoning Bitcoin. Yet the available data cannot distinguish an asset manager reducing exposure from an individual investor selling shares, or a market participant unwinding a hedged position.

It has been revealed that nor does it establish whether the capital left Bitcoin altogether or found another route back into the market. That uncertainty matters because the industry has grown comfortable treating ETF inflows as evidence of institutional conviction. Applying the opposite interpretation to withdrawals may be tempting, but it is no more conclusive.

What November demonstrated was a substantial withdrawal of capital from these investment products, led disproportionately by BlackRock’s IBIT.

Whether it represented a broader loss of faith in Bitcoin was a considerably larger question though.

And while investors were heading for the exits, there seemed to be little indication that the fund itself had stopped functioning as intended.

In a recent development, there is an understandable tendency to interpret large ETF outflows as a sign that the investment product itself has somehow failed. However, IBIT’s trading data tells us a more measured story.

According to iShares, IBIT closed at $33.02 on November 20 against a net asset value of $33.05, a discount of about 0.10%. Its 30-day median bid-ask spread was 0.02%. In other words, the fund traded almost exactly at the value of the Bitcoin it holds, even as markets were falling.

Sources indicate that trading was heavy. About 109.2 million IBIT shares changed hands on November 20, more than twice the fund’s 30-day average of about 50.1 million.

Sources indicate that that is not the same as money leaving the fund though because trading volume is not net flow. A 30-day median spread also doesn’t show that trading stayed cheap at every volatile moment.

It has been revealed that still, nothing here suggests investors were fleeing a broken product. They were trading a working fund whose underlying asset had dropped sharply. IBIT’s NAV fell $2.08 (5.92%) on November 20 to $33.05, and its NAV total return for 2026 stood at −29.06% as of November 19.

Industry observers note that wall Street made Bitcoin easier to buy. That was never the same promise as making it safer to hold. That distinction matters for the question that comes next — how much of the fall in ETF assets was money leaving, and how much was the price?

In a recent development, according to SoSoValue, combined Spot Bitcoin ETF assets reached approximately $110.8 billion on October 5. By November 20, they had fallen to roughly $71.3 billion.

A decline approaching $39.5 billion sounds extraordinary beside three weeks of approximately $4.14 billion in net withdrawals.

However, assets under management represent the market value of what these funds hold. That value changes both when investors create or redeem shares and when Bitcoin itself rises or falls.

According to recent reports, using Coinbase Bitcoin prices recorded by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, Bitcoin fell from approximately $85,821 on October 5 to $58,831 on November 20 — A fall of 31.4%.

Over the same period, reported ETF assets fell by approximately 36%.

Such a comparison strongly suggests that Bitcoin’s price decline accounted for much of the reduction in ETF asset values. It is not a precise decomposition — flows occurred throughout the period, holdings changed, and the dates and valuation methodologies must be matched before assigning an exact proportion to each driver.

Still, the broad conclusion is difficult to miss.

Sources indicate that tens of billions of dollars can disappear from reported fund asset values without an equivalent sum being withdrawn by investors. A falling portfolio value and a redeemed investment are two different financial events. Treating them interchangeably gives a dramatic headline considerably more authority than it deserves.

Bitcoin’s ETF market was not the only place seeing withdrawals either.

In a recent development, from November 9 to 13, U.S Spot Ether ETFs lost about $398.9 million, according to Farside. BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) accounted for about $311.1 million of that, or 78%. The following week, Ether funds lost about $306 million, with ETHA responsible for about $230 million or 75%.

That’s the same pattern we saw in Bitcoin — one BlackRock fund carrying most of the headline outflow.

Stablecoins told a slower story. According to DefiLlama, their combined market capitalisation was about $295.3 billion on October 30. It fell to $290.2 billion by November 6, $285.6 billion by November 13, and $281.3 billion by November 20. That is a contraction of about $14 billion, or 4.8%, in three weeks.

Unlike the ETF flows, which peaked in the final week, stablecoins shrank at a fairly steady pace — about $5.1 billion, $4.6 billion, then $4.3 billion a week.

In a recent development, stablecoins are the dollar-pegged tokens traders use for settlement, trading balances, and collateral. So, a falling supply suggests liquidity may be tightening beyond the regulated ETF market. The two trends overlapped, but they moved at different speeds.

Bitcoin’s own trading schedule adds a complication too.

FRED’s Coinbase series demonstrated Bitcoin falling from about $68,178 on November 13 to $62,891 on November 14, a drop of 7.8%, after that week’s ETF sessions ended.

Sources indicate that however, after the much heavier withdrawal week ending November 20, Bitcoin went the other way. It fell from about $58,831 on November 20 to $60,992 on November 22 — A gain of 3.7%.

Sources indicate that two weekends prove nothing on their own, and FRED’s prices are taken at 5 p.m Pacific, not at the ETF close. But they do show that a record ETF outflow and a falling price don’t move in lockstep.

There is no need to minimise the withdrawals. About $4.14 billion in three weeks is a major reversal, particularly when the final week was the worst of the three.

Nor should IBIT’s concentration be brushed off as a consequence of its size. Its 84% share of the net outflows exceeded its roughly two-thirds share of starting industry assets.

However, context changes the interpretation.

Recent findings suggest that soSoValue’s November 20 figures still showed about $52.8 billion in cumulative net inflows since January 2024. That is down roughly $4 billion from where November began, but nearly three years of accumulated inflows were not erased by three difficult weeks.

October offers a useful warning about reading any headline in isolation. The same fund that masked withdrawals elsewhere in two October weeks went on to account for most of November’s exits. The industry totals recorded both developments accurately, yet told very different stories depending on whether you looked at the funds behind them.

The ETF structure broadened access to Bitcoin. It also gave investors a familiar, liquid way to reduce exposure. Neither is a guarantee about Bitcoin’s price.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps institutions were cutting risk. Or, retail investors may have been heading for the exits. Others could simply have been unwinding complex positions that had little to do with long-term conviction in Bitcoin. All three are plausible explanations.

What they do establish is narrower but more useful — the withdrawals were substantial, heavily concentrated in one product, and increasingly shared across competing funds as November went on.

So, the next time a billion-dollar ETF outflow makes the headlines, the interesting questions begin after the headline. Which funds accounted for it? How large were the withdrawals relative to their assets? Is the number money leaving a product, or is the market value of its holdings falling?

And one more, which no flow table can answer — Who was actually selling?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andrew Webley, CEO of The Smarter Web Company, noted that Bitcoin's drop has been sharper than he had anticipated, but he does not think the digital asset's price will decline much further.

The British CEO, whose firm recently added 55 BTC to its treasury, mentioned investors' opinions on Bitcoin can shift considerably without any changes to Bitcoin itself.

"Sentiment towards Bitcoin can change very rapidly. Without Bitcoin changing at all," Webley said on X.

Webley advised investors to consider Bitcoin's movements relative to other assets. Bitcoin's price decline shows investors how much the cryptocurrency has lost in absolute terms.

However, Bitcoin's performance relative to the broader market may indicate BTC is being sold specifically or whether investors are taking profits across multiple markets. Webley did not specify which assets he was comparing Bitcoin against.

"Do I expect Bitcoin to go significantly lower from here? No. But as the past few weeks have shown, predicting short-term price movements is a very challenging task," Webley said.

Some of the most challenging periods for investors, he said, were followed by some of his most profitable periods.

His most definitive prediction concerned Bitcoin's longer-term outlook: "Bitcoin has an incredible future.".

In fact, Webley's company has been buying more Bitcoin as its price has been dropping.

On Nov. 17, Smarter Web remarked it spent around £2.75 million on 55 BTC, bringing its total holdings to 2,905 BTC.

The average purchase price was £49,991 per Bitcoin, roughly 38% below the treasury's overall average purchase price of £81,234 following the transaction.

Industry observers note that smarter Web borrowed around £2.6 million under its Coinbase credit facility to finance most of the purchase. The organization used its existing Bitcoin holdings as collateral.

Following the transaction, Smarter Web had around £19 million outstanding under the dollar-denominated credit facility.

9 rescued orangutans returned to the wild in Indonesia

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (402 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Indonesian province of West Kalimantan, on the island of Borneo, is no stranger to wildfires.
  • Earlier this year, four mother-baby orangutan pairs and one adult female orangutan (genus Pongo) were rescued from areas in Ketapang (a regency in the West Kalimantan province) impacted by the fires.
  • According to recent reports, they were taken to an orangutan rescue and rehabilitation centre in Ketapang, West Kalimantan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Indonesian province of West Kalimantan, on the island of Borneo, is no stranger to wildfires. Horrific wildfires burned in 2015 and 2019, the latter of which set ablaze around 1.6 million hectares of Indonesian forest and land. However, the scale of destruction from this year’s El Niño-intensified fires throughout the island is unprecedented, according to the nonprofit International Animal Rescue.

Earlier this year, four mother-baby orangutan pairs and one adult female orangutan (genus Pongo) were rescued from areas in Ketapang (a regency in the West Kalimantan province) impacted by the fires. They were dehydrated and malnourished, and some had burned their feet, likely because they stepped on embers as they crossed burning peatland.

According to recent reports, they were taken to an orangutan rescue and rehabilitation centre in Ketapang, West Kalimantan. The center is run by Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI), a nonprofit dedicated to primate and habitat conservation in Indonesia. YIARI’s medical team kept an eye on their recovery, and then conducted health examinations to make sure they were all ready for release. The last of these examinations revealed that three of the females were pregnant.

“Their return to the wild is therefore especially important, giving these mothers the opportunity to raise their future young in a safer forest habitat,” International Animal Rescue, YIARI’s founding partner, wrote in a statement.

Experts ultimately chose to release them at Batu Nyambu Protected Forest. While also in West Kalimantan, its roughly 23,000 hectares of land and nearby forests haven’t been affected by the recent fires. Batu Nyambu has plenty of natural food, fresh water, nesting trees, and space. But getting the females and their babies there wasn’t simple—they had to travel by road, boat, and on foot for a total of 12 hours. Luckily, they had support from local communities and traditional leaders.

“We are grateful for the support of the community, village governments and traditional leaders,” said Argitoe Ranting, YIARI’s Director of Operations. “The long-term success of conservation efforts depends not only on protecting the area, but also on the role of the people living around the forest in safeguarding habitat and preventing various threats to wildlife.”.

Most fires in Indonesia are associated with human activity such as using fire to clear land for plantations and agriculture.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you wake up tomorrow as the esteemed Lord Mayor of London, you’ll want to make a properly dignified entrance. To make sure your arrival turns the right heads, Electrogenic has taken the Mayor’s 1973 Roll-Royce Phantom VI and turned it into a properly traditional standard-bearer with modern electric power.

The stately, stylish, and silent electric Rolls-Royce car made its public debut at last month’s Salon Privé weekend at Blenheim Palace, where it joined a growing fleet of classic Rollers that have received Elctrogenic’s electric conversion, including the stunning Mulliner-bodied 1929 Phantom II that we covered back in 2023.

Industry observers note that for this project, Electrogenic carefully removed the internal combustion-based engine, transmission, and fuel system from the City of London Corporation’s official ’73 Phantom VI limo and replaced it with a 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motor putting out 310 Nm (~230 lb-ft) of torque. Sharp-eyed readers will note those numbers are significantly lower than what you’d expect from the 6.2L L410 V8 fitted with twin SU carburetors (as it was in the standard ’73 IV), but since those numbers were never officially published, we would say that the power available from the upcoming electric drivetrain is similarly adequate for Mayoral use.

Power for the electric motor comes from a 62 kWh li-ion battery fitted under the hood bonnet, and offers more than enough range to get the Lord Mayor to their appointments in and around the city.

To ensure the heads of the heads of the city don’t bob in an undignified manner while on parade, Electrogenic added a “ceremonial” drive mode that trims power and torque and softens the throttle map, so the chauffeur can more easily hold the crawling pace demanded by civic processions and state occasions.

Recent findings suggest that “We were honored to be asked to electrify this significant motor car, and to play a part in the City of London Corporation’s journey to net zero,” notes Steve Drummond, chief executive of Electrogenic. “When it was introduced in the late 1960s, the Rolls-Royce VI was the most refined and dignified limousine on the road. Now, thanks to electrification, its core character has been enhanced further: it is whisper quiet, effortless to drive with swift performance, and emits zero tailpipe emissions.”.

It's key for government to be seen to follow it's own policy.

A standard complaint by oil lobbyists is that government vehicles aren't electrified.

Industry observers note that only 374 Phantom VIs were built between 1968 and 1990, with this 3 meter-long coach-built limousine having been commissioned during the mayoralty of Alderwoman Dame Susan Langley DBE, the 697th Lord Mayor of the City of London. The Phantom was converted as part of the Corporation’s broader effort to achieve a net zero carbon emissions goal from its own operations in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Ripple (XRP) » XRP’s Price Fails To Hold $1 After a Brief Spike, But..

Institutional progress continues, but the development of Ripple’s custody service doesn’t spark up a rally.

XRP’s price briefly climbed above $1 this week, reaching roughly $1.03 before sellers pushed it back below the level within hours. The move followed a rebound from near $0.91, leaving the token trading around $0.93 to $0.96.

It has been revealed that the push above $1 was helped in part by traders closing bearish futures positions. XRP short liquidations made up a substantial share of recent XRP futures liquidations, a dynamic that can produce sharp rallies without durable buying.

Sources indicate that spot-market data has shown sellers retaining the upper hand in recent weeks, though the pace of net selling has eased. Large crypto holders accumulated an estimated $72 million in XRP over several days, standing apart from reported selling in Bitcoin and Ether (ETH).

According to recent reports, that activity has not yet turned $1 from resistance into a reliable floor. XRP was rejected around the level more than once during the latest stretch of trading.

The price weakness has continued even as Ripple expands its institutional footprint. Yapı Kredi, one of Türkiye’s largest private banks, plans to use Ripple Custody for digital-asset services connected to its crypto platform, with the infrastructure operated on the bank’s own premises.

Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin has also grown. Its circulating supply recently reached a high near $2.87 billion, briefly overtaking USD1 before subsequent redemptions put the rival token marginally back ahead.

Industry observers note that 💵 Ripple's RLUSD has overtaken Trump-linked USD1 by circulating supply, hitting a record $2.87B. Ripple's stablecoin keeps growing, even in a bear market. The onchain dollar keeps growing. This is where real adoption is happening.#RLUSD #Ripple #Stablecoins.

About $761 million of RLUSD supply is held on the XRP Ledger, where XRP is used to pay transaction fees.

Those developments strengthen Ripple’s broader payments, custody and stablecoin business, but they do not automatically create immediate buying pressure for XRP.

Turkish XRP trading against the lira, for example, has fallen sharply from year-earlier levels despite the bank custody announcement.

XRP’s price has lost about 26% over the past month and remains well below its longer-term trend averages. The altcoin now trades just one cent above the low-tier Bollinger Band (BOLL).

A break above the recent high near $1.03 could bring the $1.04 to $1.08 area into view, while failure to hold the $0.91 to $0.92 support zone could expose $0.86.

Ripple’s institutional progress may matter over a longer horizon, but XRP investors are still waiting for that momentum to show up decisively in the market.

Bitcoin ‘As Vital as It’s Ever Been’ if Inflation Rises, Coinbase CEO Notes

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (398 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that "Bitcoin investors tend to sell BTC when there's a massive IPO.
  • That's Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong's take on Bitcoin investor behavior, less than a week after the record-breaking $93.5 billion IPO of Claude creator Anthropic.
  • "Historically, people rotate out of it to take advantage of a significant IPO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that "Bitcoin investors tend to sell BTC when there's a massive IPO. Then they come back.".

That's Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong's take on Bitcoin investor behavior, less than a week after the record-breaking $93.5 billion IPO of Claude creator Anthropic.

"Historically, people rotate out of it to take advantage of a significant IPO. Then they come back in," Armstrong wrote on X earlier today.

The limited window of opportunity to invest in an IPO helps explain the behavior Armstrong described. For an investor to buy at the IPO price, there's only a certain period during which they can request an allocation of shares. After that, the price is determined by the market.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 19, Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq, and that brief window of opportunity mattered.

Shares were priced at $83, up from the $70-$78 range indicated just two days earlier. Anthropic's stock, trading under the ticker ANT, opened at $111.50.

If you bought at that opening price, you paid about 34% more per share than an investor who received an allocation at the IPO price.

When the IPO closed on Nov. 20, 1.127 billion shares had been sold, including 147 million additional shares purchased by underwriters exercising their option.

Recent findings suggest that of the $93.5 billion in gross proceeds, Anthropic itself received around $91.6 billion. The rest went to existing shareholders.

It has been revealed that there was also a separate $26 billion private placement involving investors such as Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and others. In total, the combined transactions were valued at $119.5 billion.

As for the longer-term case for holding BTC, Armstrong's point concerns investors' expectations about the future purchasing power of their money.

"If you think there is going to be more inflation and money printing in the future, bitcoin is as important as ever.".

At the heart of the matter is Bitcoin's 21 million supply limit.

In a recent development, if you expect governments to continue expanding the money supply, you may still be excited by the prospect of a major IPO. And you may sell some of your BTC to participate in it.

Armstrong's argument is that the window of opportunity to participate in a major IPO eventually closes.

However, the reasons investors bought Bitcoin in the first place may remain long after the newly listed stock starts trading.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to the report, the ETF has seen net cash flows of $667 million since it began trading on the NYSE in November 2025.
  • In essence, despite XRP’s lackluster performance, interest in the ETF continues to receive institutional investment, implying a high level of investor demand.
  • Sources indicate that in a post on X, Bitwise highlighted XRP’s decade-long presence in the crypto market.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitwise has released its annual XRP ETF report.

According to the report, the ETF has seen net cash flows of $667 million since it began trading on the NYSE in November 2025. Meanwhile, assets under management were in excess of $376 million while total trading crossed $3.5 billion, averaging around $14 million a day.

In essence, despite XRP’s lackluster performance, interest in the ETF continues to receive institutional investment, implying a high level of investor demand.

Sources indicate that in a post on X, Bitwise highlighted XRP’s decade-long presence in the crypto market. It also noted how the asset has remained relevant through multiple market cycles and continues to shape the industry’s future.

XRP has been part of crypto’s story for more than a decade, through every cycle, and it’s still helping shape what comes next. We’re grateful to everyone who’s been part of the journey so far. Here’s to year two!

The timing is particularly interesting here.

Bitwise’s report comes as XRP’s technical and on-chain metrics continue to deteriorate. Meanwhile, prediction markets are also increasingly pricing in a year-end target below $0.80. Against this backdrop, the key question is whether Bitwise’s report can strengthen institutional interest and turn the current bearish setup into a bear trap.

The impact of Bitwise’s one-year XRP ETF performance could already be triggering FOMO.

Notably, another Wall Street firm has disclosed exposure to an XRP ETF. Atlanta-based Arkadios Wealth Advisors, which looks after $8.79 billion in client assets, stated this in its most recent SEC document.

Furthermore, there is some institutional interest in Turkiye too. One of the nation’s biggest private banks, Yapi Kredi, is leveraging Ripple Custody to provide digital asset security solutions.

The key takeaway? XRP’s derivatives continue to be significantly net short, with the long/short ratio showing a pronounced sell-side sentiment. At the time of writing, XRP seemed set to close its 10th consecutive weekly down candle, with broader market FUD and prediction markets pricing in a year-end target below $0.80 to reinforce the cautious outlook.

Interestingly, however, the XRP/BTC ratio has risen by almost 5% following three successive weeks of upside.

In essence, broader market weakness could create room for more capital to flow into XRP.

This makes it an vital setup to watch over the coming months. The logic is simple —  Entering Q4, market participants are already factoring in further downside potential. In this context, Bitwise’s recent report, growing ETF exposure, and Ripple’s expansion in Turkiye could encourage further capital rotation into XRP.

If this trend continues, XRP’s ongoing consolidation around $0.90 could turn out to be an accumulation phase before a potential bear trap.

Bitwise’s XRP ETF has attracted $667 million in net inflows, while growing institutional exposure and Ripple’s expansion in Turkiye point to sustained demand.

Despite bearish derivatives and weakening market sentiment, rising XRP/BTC strength could signal a potential accumulation phase.

The 10 Best Fitness Trackers, Tested by Our Fitness and Tech Experts
