In a recent development, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

IT’s AN OFT-EXPRESSED sentiment, but it’s true: The holidays turn people’s attention toward friends, family, and community. There’s a beauty in the selfless, caring gifts people give to others. And while all that giving feels great, the holidays are also a good time to treat yourself. Plus, it’s getting colder.

In a recent development, whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself). The brand has jackets and accessories with familiar winter looks, as well as products with less expected silhouettes that still offer protection from the elements in an understated style.

Here’s a look at some of the best cold-weather gear that will have you wrapping up the gift of warmth and durability… even if that gift is for yourself.

This is an easy gifting win because the warm, hooded, insulated jacket is a recognizable The North Face staple, evoking an unpretentious spin on the brand’s iconic Nuptse Jacket.

It’s familiar, but it’s also practical—the kind of gift you feel good about because it’s going to get a ton of use. (And it can withstand the repeated wears.) The attached hood offers protection from biting winds, and the straightforward color options make it easy to pair with a variety of outfits, whether it’s something fun or part of a heavy bundling during the coldest days of winter. This is the perfect type of winter coat: warm but not too puffy.

Industry observers note that the Zaneck Jacket is a great alternative to the Aconcagua, stepping away from the outdoorsy look the brand is best known for. It’s still waterproof and insulated, but it has a longer, more modern cut.

The Zaneck comes with a removable faux fur lining for the hood, which, in addition to being warm, means there are a couple of different looks that can be teased out of it. The straight cuffs add to its stylish feel in a way that doesn’t scream “I’m dressed for warmth and not fashion,” even though it’s doing both.

The Lone Peak Triclimate 2 has a lot in common with the Zaneck. From a distance, they cut a similar silhouette. However, the Lone Peak adds a little versatility if you’re looking for a jacket that can handle a variety of climates.

A removable, insulated inner jacket is attached to a removable, insulated top layer, which is fit for rainy conditions or as a spring or fall jacket. The insulated layer converts the whole thing into a winter-ready jacket. It also sports underarm vents capable of releasing heat in the middle of a long hike, ideal for outdoorsy types. The hood is removable and it’s got adjustable cuffs and an adjustable hem, making this a do-it-all jacket.

The lightweight aspect makes this the kind of coat you toss in the backseat on the way to a hike, just in case. It’s also great for layering, whether it’s tossed on over a sweater or layered under an overcoat to make a favorite jacket more winter-ready.

Recent findings suggest that this edition of the classic Base Camp Duffel echoes the design details we love in The North Face’s jackets. While it’s got enough style and a heap of color options for daily use, it’s built for adventure.

Recent findings suggest that made with water- and tear-resistant fabric, it boasts 71 liters of storage space, a roomier option to the similar 31-liter version. Like all of the brand’s products, it’s built as if the designers have been through the rigors of outdoor adventures (and they probably have). It’s got a sweeping D-zip opening, backpack straps, mesh pockets, and compression straps in case you’re curious if you can pack 73 liters worth of gear into the 71-liter space. (You know you’ve tried.).

Recent findings suggest that the North Face has a lot of hats, none more iconic than this. The Salty Lined Beanie has a classic feel, fitting snuggly over the head with rib-knit texture, a cuffed shape, soft fabric, and ample color options to ensure it will match any jacket or accessory. The Salty Lined Beanie encapsulates the entire The North Face vibe in a small way: It’s stylish enough for a subway ride to work and practical enough for an outdoor adventure. Best of all, it’ll keep your ears warm in either instance.

Recent findings suggest that often, the best glove is the one that disappears into the outfit. It looks seamless, keeping hands warm without drawing too much attention. The Etip Recycled Glove is about functionality first and foremost, but the simple design and understated colors makes it look good with a variety of winter outfits.

While we all like to pretend we aren’t attached to our phones, the Etip makes a great modern gift because its stretchy fleece delivers a snug fit and the palms have touchscreen compatibility. That means you won’t have to take off your gloves to respond to that notable text while the snow is falling.

  • Industry observers note that BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT), Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund, began trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange on November 26, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Switzerland’s First Spot Bitcoin ETF BBIT Begins Trading on SIX.

BIT Asset Management’s regulated fund brings direct spot Bitcoin access to Swiss retail accounts.

Industry observers note that BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT), Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund, began trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange on November 26, 2026. Structured as a regulated Swiss collective investment fund, the product gives retail investors direct Bitcoin exposure through standard Swiss bank or brokerage accounts without self-custody.

The passive fund tracks the SIX Bitcoin Reference Rate and holds physical Bitcoin offline in cold storage at regulated Swiss custodian AMINA Bank AG, ring-fenced from the manager’s and custodian’s own assets.

BIT Asset Management describes BBIT as Europe’s currently active spot Bitcoin ETF, though public offering is approved only in Switzerland.

Industry observers note that BBIT is listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and trades in both U.S. dollars and Swiss francs, with a target annual management fee of 0.19%. The fund launched with an initial concern price of $10 per unit and an allocation of 350 BTC, valued at more than $20 million at launch.

Switzerland’s Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) approved BBIT’s fund contract on October 20, 2026, following an 18-month review.

FINMA granted an exemption from standard investment diversification requirements, allowing the fund to invest exclusively in Bitcoin based on the cryptocurrency’s established trading history and liquidity.

However, the fund is classified as an alternative investment fund with specific risks, reflecting Bitcoin’s volatility and potential for substantial capital losses.

Sources indicate that unlike most European crypto exchange-traded products, which are structured as debt instruments and expose investors to issuer credit risk, BBIT operates under Swiss collective investment scheme legislation. This means investors hold fund units backed by ring-fenced assets, legally separated from the fund management company’s own assets.

Pernet von Ballmoos AG (PvB) acts as the fund management company and issuer, while BIT Asset Management serves as the sponsor and investment manager. Flow Traders has been appointed as the market maker, supporting secondary-market liquidity.

The fund also provides daily disclosure of its Bitcoin holdings and supports in-kind subscriptions for eligible institutional participants.

It has been revealed that while BBIT is Switzerland’s first retail spot Bitcoin ETF, a physically backed Bitcoin product—the Jacobi FT Wilshire Bitcoin ETF—previously debuted on Euronext Amsterdam in August 2023 before Euronext listed it as inactive in February 2026 and liquidation proceedings began later that month. Meanwhile, SIX has hosted physically backed crypto ETPs since 2019.

The listing arrives with Bitcoin price hovering near $60,500 after heavy November outflows across U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.

BIT—formerly known as Matrixport—expanded its Swiss fund footprint after acquiring and rebranding its Swiss asset management arm (originally rooted in Crypto Finance Asset Management).

This approval is a major step for Switzerland, as it allows everyday investors to gain direct exposure to Bitcoin through a regulated Swiss investment fund. It also highlights that regulators are becoming more open to Bitcoin as a mainstream investment asset.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toobit, the award-winning global cryptocurrency exchange, today reports that its zero-slippage trading service delivered 474,904 USDT in net slippage subsidies between July 1 and October 27, 2026, with 3,766 trading accounts receiving positive subsidies during the period.

Industry observers note that slippage is an often-overlooked trading cost that occurs when an order is filled at a different price than expected. Unlike trading fees, slippage can be difficult to anticipate, particularly during rapid market movements. By reducing unfavorable price differences, traders can better manage their trading costs and keep more of their potential returns.

In a recent development, to help traders address this challenge, Toobit offers its guaranteed price (GTD price) feature for eligible perpetual futures orders. The feature supports take-profit (TP) and stop-loss (SL) settings, with GTD TP targeting fills at the trigger price or better and GTD SL helping protect against unfavorable slippage.

For futures traders, this protection can be particularly valuable during volatile conditions. A conventional stop-loss market order may fill at a price below its trigger when prices fall rapidly, increasing losses beyond the intended level. Guaranteed price helps address this risk by allowing eligible stop-loss orders to close at their preset prices.

Sources indicate that traders can access guaranteed price on supported perpetual futures pairs, subject to eligibility requirements, fees, and execution exceptions. Traders can explore Toobit Futures or learn more through the guaranteed price feature guide.

Sources indicate that toobit is where the future of crypto trading unfolds. The award-winning cryptocurrency derivatives exchange provides zero-fee spot trading, AI trading tools, and high leverage for both crypto and TradFi markets. Built for those who thrive on exploring upcoming frontiers, Toobit maintains a fair, secure, and transparent environment for traders to navigate digital asset markets.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells?
  • Sources indicate that unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.

Recent findings suggest that how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells? According to Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, who is also leading its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, the answer lies in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology.

Sources indicate that unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs. They also typically hold up better after years of use and charging.

To make it a reality, Ford turned to CATL, the leading global EV battery manufacturer. Ford uses CATL’s licensed technology and manufacturing expertise at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant.

Ford said it will be the first in the US to deliver LFP batteries for mainstream automotive use, with the battery cells now rolling off the line in Michigan.

The first LFP battery cells are headed to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant and will be used to power Fathom prototypes, its first vehicle based on the UEV platform.

Ford designed and engineered the Fathom from the ground up for efficiency. As such, it chose prismatic battery cells because they fit directly into the chassis, reducing structural costs.

With cells now being delivered from a plant that it owns and operates, Ford mentioned it will use the knowledge gained in Michigan to support more affordable EVs and Ford Energy, its upcoming battery energy storage business in Kentucky.

At Ford’s new battery plant in Michigan, assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, making it one of the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China.

Although the accelerated output drives down costs, Ford stated employees use AI-powered image recognition and inspection tools to spot defects in real time and maintain quality.

“Our goal is to make defective cells so rare that we track their frequency per billion cells rather than per million,” Ford said.

With production testing now underway, Ford intends to have the battery pack plant in Michigan up and running in 2027, ahead of schedule.

Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range model.

CEO Jim Farley mentioned on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last month that the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle based on the UEV platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.

In a recent development, farley said the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and still affordable. The starting MSRP is under $30,000, and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today’s market, he added.

According to recent reports, ford and Slate both producing vehicles with US-produced LFP batteries is a great milestone. Hopefully we can keep pushing our domestic battery supply chain forward.

Ford mentioned the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and it will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.

It has been revealed that the pickup will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps directly into the navigation system. All versions will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving, with standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.

Although we have yet to see it, Ford noted the Fathom features a “large touchscreen display” with easy-to-use navigation.

Ford has not revealed battery specs or range, but we do know the pickup will have an NACS port after several prototypes were spotted at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.

As the total number of burn transactions approaches the 22,000 mark, Shiba Inu’s token-burning activity is nearing another significant milestone.

It has been revealed that the number of SHIB burn transactions right now stands at 21,991, with only nine transactions to go to reach the 22,000 milestone, according to Shibburn. In total, these transactions have burned 410,845,372,884,899 SHIB.

This is a testament to the continuing efforts by the SHIB community to reduce the cryptocurrency’s massive circulating supply by sending tokens to unreachable wallet addresses. The tokens are sent to these dead wallets and are then permanently out of circulation.

Shiba Inu began with an initial supply of approximately one quadrillion tokens. Since then, over 410.8 trillion SHIB tokens have been burned, meaning that 41.08% of the original supply of 1 quadrillion tokens has been destroyed. But individual burns have very different effects. Some transactions are for relatively small amounts, while others remove millions or even billions of SHIB from circulation.

The milestone is another sign of the community’s ongoing interest in Shiba Inu’s tokenomics as investors look for developments that could create stronger demand across the ecosystem.

The daily burn rate of Shiba Inu has seen a huge spike of 443%, as the SHIB community continues its attempt to shrink the circulating supply of the cryptocurrency.

Sources indicate that A higher burn rate indicates more tokens have been destroyed than on the previous day. According to Shibburn, 4.40 million SHIB have been burned in the last 24 hours, with the daily burn rate jumping 443%. This contributes to a total of 8.42 million SHIB burned in the last seven days and 322.85 million SHIB sent to dead wallets in the last 30 days.

According to recent reports, despite these cumulative burns, SHIB’s price performance still depends on broader market conditions and investor demand. At the time of writing, SHIB was up 5.60% in the last 24 hours to $0.00000364 amid the Thanksgiving holiday and down 6.45% weekly.

#134154. Peeping woodcocks are evolutionary oddballs

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (514 w)

Peeping woodcocks are evolutionary oddballs

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet.
  • Sources indicate that woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances.
  • “The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, noted in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As far as birds go, the eight known species of woodcock (genus Scolopax) look like they specifically evolved to go viral on the internet. You’ve probably seen at least a few videos of the birds on social media darting across beaches and being incredibly vocal. As if their small, squat bodies and comically long beaks weren’t enough, they also vocalize with distinctively cartoonish peeping tweets during their mating displays.

Sources indicate that woodcocks are part of the larger sandpiper family, but unlike their migratory relatives, most only travel extremely short seasonal distances. Six of the eight species are only found on specific islands, and some of them don’t even migrate at all. So how did these evolutionary oddballs even get their start—and stop migrating? To piece together their unique avian story, biologists analyzed the DNA of all eight woodcock species and 22 species of snipe.

“The distribution of woodcocks and snipes around the world is really unusual,” John Bates, the curator of birds at the Field Museum’s Negaunee Integrative Research Center in Chicago, noted in a statement. “They’re not terribly aerodynamic, and yet they’ve clearly gotten around.”.

Bates and his colleagues published the results of their work today in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS). The years-long endeavor involved not only examining preserved woodcock specimens housed in the Field Museum, but a fossilized sandpiper previously excavated from a cave site in Haiti. The remains found on the island of Hispaniola are around 1,000 years old, but that is still extremely young in the grand history of shorebirds.

Sources indicate that the earliest members of the sandpiper family began in the northern hemisphere before slowly migrating to islands along lower latitudes. Those birds subsequently migrated much shorter distances after settling in the warmer climates. However, they didn’t remain sedentary. Based on the DNA analysis detailed in their study, Bates and his team theorize that snipes from Africa eventually traveled across the Atlantic Ocean, then evolved into newly introduced species in South America. From there, more of the birds made their way over the Pacific Ocean to New Zealand.

Their examinations also cleared up a bit of confusion. Biologists initially believed the fossilized sandpiper from Haiti was a woodcock, but the most recent data now shows that it’s a snipe.

It has been revealed that “Snipes and woodcocks have been around for 20 to 25 million years,” Bates explained. “Over that time, as newly introduced species have evolved and moved around the world, their migratory patterns have changed, too.”.

These changes are likely to continue amid today’s dramatic climate shifts, but that may pose a problem for the beloved woodcocks.

According to recent reports, “These are definitely birds that would be affected by changing habitats and changing climates,” mentioned Bates. “Some of these woodcocks are found only in the mountain forests on islands between Asia and Australia, and if those forests get cut down, the birds are going to be gone too.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Blitz news » MetaMask Brings Stablecoin Payments to Three Asian Markets With Fresh Card Launch.

MetaMask expands its payment card to Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam for Mastercard transactions.

Cryptocurrency wallet provider MetaMask released its payment card in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam on November 25, allowing users to spend its dollar-pegged mUSD stablecoin at merchants that accept Mastercard.

The move gives owners in the three markets another way to use stablecoins for everyday purchases. Rather than transferring funds to a centralized cryptocurrency exchange before spending them, users can make payments directly through a card linked to their MetaMask wallet.

MetaMask Card uses mUSD, a US dollar-pegged stablecoin, to make payments at merchants that accept Mastercard. People can pay online with their virtual card or in stores through Apple Pay and Google Pay. At checkout, the required amount of mUSD is converted into the local currency, such as Japanese yen.

In a recent development, in Japan, the card is available only as a virtual version and carries no annual fee. ATM cash withdrawals are not supported. Consumers can spend up to $10,000 per transaction and $15,000 per day.

Payments made with an mUSD balance at domestic merchants carry no transaction fee, while purchases at merchants outside the user’s country of residence incur a 1% fee.

To apply, users must access the Money tab in the MetaMask mobile app, register an email address and phone number, complete identity verification (KYC), and provide proof of residence.

It has been revealed that however, the card does not support direct payments with every cryptocurrency held in MetaMask. Customers must first convert assets such as USDC into mUSD before adding funds to their MetaMask Money account.

Sources indicate that the Japanese cards are issued by Fresh Zealand-based financial services provider Immersve Limited. MetaMask states its Money account retains a self-custodial structure, allowing consumers to maintain control of their private keys.

The expansion comes as stablecoin activity continues to grow across Southeast Asia, where digital assets are increasingly used for cross-border payments and transfers.

Chainalysis’s 2026 regional research reveals that Thailand and Vietnam, alongside the Philippines, accounted for 14.4% of global small-value peer-to-peer transfers. The report also found that cross-border stablecoin activity exceeded domestic volumes in both countries, reaching $10.4 billion in Thailand and $6.9 billion in Vietnam.

Japan offers a different opportunity. Its developing regulatory framework and growing interest in stablecoins provide another market for MetaMask to test whether crypto wallets can become practical payment tools.

Industry observers note that metaMask first tested its payment card in the UK and Europe in August 2024 before launching it to US customers in February 2026. The service has since expanded to the European Economic Area, Canada, and parts of Central and South America.

KuCoin will delist Monero (XMR) on Nov. 30, the exchange unveiled on Thursday. XMR dropped as low as $436 after the announcement and lost almost 15% within four hours, according to Kraken data on TradingView.

In the notice, KuCoin remarked that XMR would be delisted "in accordance with the Special Treatment Rules of KuCoin." The exchange closed XMR deposits on Thursday and will remove the XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC pairs at 08:00 UTC on Nov. 30.

KuCoin will also shut down XMR trading bots, Convert swaps and Earn products before the delisting. Users can withdraw XMR until Dec. 31, and KuCoin noted that it could close withdrawals earlier if the Monero network stops producing blocks or processing transfers.

On Thursday, KuCoin's XMR/USDT pair had $73.8 million in 24-hour volume, according to CoinMarketCap. It was the largest Monero spot market and accounted for 47% of XMR spot trading. HTX's XMR/USDT pair was second with $29.5 million.

In a recent development, kuCoin did not mention its XMRUSDT perpetual contract in the notice. The contract had $33 million in 24-hour volume on Thursday, according to CoinMarketCap. Binance had the largest XMR perpetual market with $89.3 million.

PerpetualCow, who promotes the Wagyu trading platform on X, also responded to the delisting. "Over 50% of customers sourced their XMR indirectly from KuCoin; it fuelled ALL instant swap exchanges," he wrote on Thursday. According to PerpetualCow, instant swap services "don't have their own liquidity" and "simply wrapped around KuCoin and sold/bought into their order books.".

Recent findings suggest that in the same post, he wrote that Wagyu had done more than $1.5 billion in volume in less than a year. He also shared a screenshot of Wagyu's XMR-USDC market together with the post, and it demonstrated $63.5 million in 24-hour volume.

Earlier in November, the MEXC exchange also delisted XMR. The exchange removed XMR spot and perpetual markets on Nov. 13.

Sources indicate that OKX delisted XMR in January 2024, and Binance removed the coin on Feb. 20, 2024. Binance said at the time that it would conduct a deeper review "when a coin or token no longer meets this standard, or the industry changes." XMR fell more than 15% after the Binance announcement.

Kraken stopped XMR trading for clients in the European Economic Area at the end of October 2024. In August 2025, Kraken revealed an XMR delisting for Canadian clients "due to recent compliance requirements in Canada" and disabled trading for them on Sept. 2, 2025.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

1Password confirmed a breach on the 25th of November after an attacker copied customer records through compromised backend systems.

It has been revealed that the manufacturer mentioned password vaults remained protected, while the stolen information raised the risk of convincing impersonation attempts. For those unaware, 1Password is a password manager that stores passwords, passkeys, and other sensitive information in encrypted digital vaults.

Industry observers note that 1Password began investigating on the 19th of November after an attacker compromised an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker used that access to push malicious code into backend services and download records for some customers.

It has been revealed that those included names, email addresses, account identifiers, creation and sign-in times, and non-secret technical metadata. The attacker also copied public keys, authentication parameters, and tokens from certain invitation, provisioning, and account recovery links.

1Password said those tokens alone could not grant access; users also needed to complete sign-in or email verification. The attacker also copied private source code and accessed the manufacturer’s software deployment systems.

However, it stated that it never stored account passwords or Secret Keys required to decrypt vaults.

Recent findings suggest that the tech giant disabled the compromised account and rotated potentially exposed credentials. It reported no internal evidence of account takeovers through exposed provisioning tokens.

The reassurance about vaults left a separate question hanging: how had one employee account enabled such extensive access?

Akash Network founder Greg Osuri said his trust was “heavily diminished” and called for an option to keep vaults entirely local. Crypto and blockchain CTO Nicki Sanders focused on the intrusion, stating,.

The part that worries me is how they got in.

Trading Strategy co-founder Mikko Ohtamaa favored open-source alternatives, arguing that transparency could make persistent attacks easier to detect.

Others were less categorical. X user Tom Lombardi called the incident,.

Industry observers note that the disagreement extended to passwords themselves. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) urged customers to change all passwords.

After 1Password remarked passwords remained unexposed, CZ acknowledged the clarification and suggested weak-password checks and changing login emails to protect against phishing.

Stolen account details could help scammers impersonate 1Password through convincing recovery messages. That risk already reaches beyond email.

Unit 42 research tracked fake IT-support voice calls targeting over 150 employees across at least ten companies. The activity ran between January and April 2026.

Binance’s official risk account previously documented WhatsApp impersonators using supposed P2P account problems to solicit login QR-code scans. Ledger’s campaign tracker documented fake support calls and physical letters directing recipients toward recovery-phrase theft.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, over the past 17 months, the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Bronx Zoo in Latest York City has rescued dozens of parrots from the illegal pet trade. They include white-fronted Amazons (Amazona albifrons) and orange-fronted conures (Eupsittula canicularis).

The United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months. All of the birds were discovered at the U.S.–Mexico border.

Sources indicate that “These animals were stolen from the wild and are victims of the illegal wildlife pet trade, and our responsibility is to give them the best possible chance for a healthy future,” Chuck Cerbini, WCS Bronx Zoo Curator of Ornithology, said in a statement. “Working with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, our veterinary and animal care teams provide specialized expertise to assess, treat, and care for confiscated wildlife.”.

When confiscated wildlife arrives at the Bronx Zoo, the veterinary and animal care teams first conduct a health check, provide any necessary medical treatment, and then help find long-term placements for those that can’t be released into the wild.

White-fronted Amazons are native to parts of Mexico and Central America and represent the smallest Amazon parrot. They are also one of the few parrot species in which males and females feature visibly different plumage. Both sexes have a white foreheads, red faces, and yellowish bills, but males have red shoulders and females have green shoulders.

Orange-fronted conures, also known as half-moon conure or Petz’s conure, are also native to parts of Mexico and Central America, where they live in open woodlands, forest edges, and savannas. They have an orange forehead and green and blue feathers.

In a recent development, the IUCN Red List categorizes both birds as a species of Least Concern, but that still  doesn’t justify trafficking them in the illegal pet trade. Parrots throughout Latin America are subject to both the loss of forest habitat and poaching.

Birds in particular l are especially threatened by trafficking because they are valued in the pet trade and the collector trade.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint.
  • It has been revealed that the result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door.
  • In the shop’s fresh video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

It has been revealed that the result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

In the shop’s fresh video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first. WCC had previously built the same client a Chevelle with a substantial gas engine.

In a recent development, friedlinghaus, who drives a Tesla himself, decided against pulling the Model 3’s motors and battery out and fitting them into the old Chevy. Instead, the Tesla stays whole and the Chevy becomes the body kit.

That’s a formula WCC has used for years with gas cars. The shop calls it “old school meets latest school”: an old GTO body on a new GTO, an old Camaro on a new Camaro, an old Mustang on a new Mustang. B-Zero is the first time it did it with a Tesla underneath.

“It sounds easy, but that process was tedious,” Friedlinghaus remarked.

Before any Chevy sheet metal went on, the crew took the bare Model 3 skateboard for a spin on the streets around the shop, with no doors, no lights and no seatbelts. Friedlinghaus joked about how many safety violations they were racking up. But it drove fine.

According to recent reports, the real headache was the wheelbase. A 1955 Chevy rides on a 115-inch wheelbase, while the Model 3 sits at 113.2 inches. On its gas builds, WCC can cut, shorten or lengthen the newer car’s frame to match the old body. You can’t do that with a Tesla, since the floor is the battery pack.

So the shop changed the body instead, stretching the Bel Air’s rear wheel wells so the wheels sit where they look like they belong.

According to recent reports, the client wanted the exterior to read as a mostly stock Bel Air. The original car was red, so WCC kept it red, with a satin finish and gloss black accents.

Inside, it’s a Model 3. The shop kept the Tesla’s interior, including the steering wheel and center touchscreen, and modified it to fit the Chevy body. The seats got black suede with white stitching in an octagon pattern that Friedlinghaus mentioned was borrowed from the Lamborghini Urus, plus red accents and a “B-Zero” script on the dash.

In a recent development, friedlinghaus said the goal was for people to see “a really nice Bel Air” from the outside, then open the door and find a Tesla. He also expects some double takes when it pulls into a Supercharger station.

It has been revealed that he admits the reaction has been split. Plenty of people are mad that the shop electrified a Bel Air, and plenty of others think it came out great. The client is clearly in the second camp, describing the car as easy to drive and saying every trip in it feels like an event.

Here’s the full build video from West Coast Customs:.

It has been revealed that this is sick. I know Tesla doesn’t care about personal car ownership anymore, but they should really sell their platform so shops can do these conversions without using salvage vehicles.

According to recent reports, well I was really interested in this build until I read how they kept it entirely Tesla inside. Not at all what I was thinking or what I'd call a true old car conversion to EV. Instead, they simply transformed the outside of a Tesla into an old looking car. To me, even the outside looks too far removed from the original Bel Air and more like a street rod. If that's what the owner wants and paid for, great.

In a recent development, but for me, I would never do a conversion like that. I really want to convert an older 70's or 80's or early 90's Cadillac into an EV. But for me, I will insist that the outside and inside look 100% like the original car with just an EV powertrain.

Don’t get me wrong, if you can recycle a salvage, that’s good, but it can’t always be done.

Compare it to the 1966 Mustang that a Sacramento Tesla parts shop converted earlier this year. That project took about $40,000 and two years, with the team grafting sections of a Model 3 floor into the Mustang. It’s an amazing build, but it’s a lot of custom engineering. WCC’s approach skips most of that. You keep Tesla’s crash structure, battery thermal management, software, over-the-air updates and Supercharger access, because you never took the car apart in the first place. It’s closer to what S-Klub did with its Model 3-based Mercedes 300SL than a traditional drivetrain swap.

The purists will hate it. That’s fine. This Bel Air will get driven more in a year than most restored ones get driven in a decade.

Recent findings suggest that solana is four days away from matching a record last seen in 2022. SOL has lost 25.7% in November so far (as of Nov. 26). That's likely to become the cryptocurrency's ninth losing month this year. If December also ends in the red, that would bring the total to 10, the highest number of losing months in a single year in SOL's history.

In a recent development, in terms of percentage losses, 2022 was overwhelmingly the worst year for Solana. SOL lost 94.15% in 2022. So far in 2026, it's down 43.09%.

SOL declined every month between January and July. August brought a 41.5% surge, followed by another 14.56% gain in September. Then, October and November erased all those gains.

Industry observers note that as of Nov. 26, Bitcoin had fallen roughly 21% in November. That provides some context. In October, BTC dropped 7.32%, while SOL lost 19%. Solana was already underperforming Bitcoin before November's losses accelerated.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, another source of demand is faltering. U.S. spot Solana ETFs have recorded $164 million in net outflows over the 30 trading days leading up to Nov. 25.

On Nov. 6, investors withdrew about $24 million from these funds. By Nov. 25, when SOL was trading around $70, the funds recorded zero net inflows. Lower prices had not yet brought ETF investors back in significant numbers.

Solana's network activity actually grew during the summer rally. Quarterly trading volume on decentralized exchanges (DEXs) increased 23% from the previous quarter to $197 billion in Q3.

Industry observers note that of that, a record $7.1 billion came from tokenized equities. That's roughly 3.6% of the quarter's total volume.

In a recent development, much of the third-quarter growth came from memecoins, according to Bitwise. On Nov. 26, the memecoin platform Pump accounted for $1.29 million of the $2.69 million in daily protocol revenue on Solana tracked by DefiLlama.

For SOL to recover and break even in November, it would need to rise about 34.6% by Nov. 30.

If November ends in the red, even a small decline in December would give Solana a record 10th losing month of the year.

Sources indicate that december ended lower in five of the last six years shown on the chart. However, six data points aren't much to base a forecast on.

  • Industry observers note that under the blueprint, a fintech or technology organization could still hold the largest individual stake, as the Financial Services Commission (FSC) outlined on Nov.
  • The legislative proposal calls stablecoins digital payment tokens and defines them as assets pegged to one currency and used mainly for payments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Korea’s financial regulator proposed limiting initial domestic stablecoin issuance to licensed groups in which banks collectively own more than 50%.

Industry observers note that under the blueprint, a fintech or technology organization could still hold the largest individual stake, as the Financial Services Commission (FSC) outlined on Nov. 24.

The legislative proposal calls stablecoins digital payment tokens and defines them as assets pegged to one currency and used mainly for payments. Issuers would put the tokens into circulation at an equivalent value in the underlying currency and would be barred from paying holders interest.

Recent findings suggest that A domestic issuer would need an FSC license and at least 5 billion won in equity capital. Applicants would have to show they have the staff and facilities to operate, submit a viable business blueprint, and explain how they would prevent conflicts of interest.

Major shareholders and executives would also have to meet eligibility requirements.

The issuer would also need FSC approval for its issuance proposal, including how many tokens it intended to issue, the maximum it could issue, how it would manage reserves, and how holders could redeem their tokens.

When a holder asked to redeem, the issuer would have to pay the equivalent value in currency without delay.

Industry observers note that to meet those requests, issuers would keep reserves worth at least 100% of outstanding issuance with a reserve manager such as a bank. The proposal would shield the reserves from third-party seizure or setoff.

Under the proposed redemption rules, the institution managing the reserves could pay holders directly if the issuer went bankrupt, lost its license, or could no longer handle normal issuance and redemption after a disruption such as a hack.

The FSC claims holders would have priority when the reserve manager makes those payments.

Sources indicate that under South Korea’s FSC proposal, issuers would have to redeem on request. Reserve managers could pay holders directly in specified cases.

Issuers would have to hold reserves worth at least 100% of outstanding tokens with an institution such as a bank.

The diagram reflects the stablecoin redemption rules in the FSC’s Nov. 24, 2026 legislative proposal.

In a recent development, each connector shows the direction of a redemption payment. The label on each path distinguishes the issuer’s duty from the reserve manager’s direct payout role.

It has been revealed that the diagram reflects the stablecoin redemption rules in the FSC’s Nov. 24, 2026 legislative proposal.

Overseas issuers would have a separate route to offer issuance and redemption in South Korea. An issuer would need adequate supervision in its home jurisdiction and a Korean branch with sufficient operating funds. It would have to register with the FSC and file separately for its foreign-issued tokens.

Platforms could only list tokens with the applicable approval or filing. The same requirement would apply to digital asset firms that trade, broker, or hold those tokens in custody.

The FSC said it would support deliberations in the National Assembly, while a later presidential decree would set detailed shareholder rules for domestic stablecoin issuers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rivian’s new electric bike spinoff, ALSO, has hit another speed bump. The manufacturer has announced that it is temporarily halting deliveries of its TM-B electric bicycles after discovering software-related problems affecting some bikes, including complications with charging behavior.

And unfortunately, this isn’t entirely surprising. We’ve already reported on some strange battery behavior with the upcoming e-bikes, as well as customers having to send their bikes back for repairs.

In a message sent to customers, ALSO explained that it was pausing shipments to address several software problems before more bikes reach riders.

“We’ve identified a few software-based concerns, such as charging behavior, that are impacting some bikes,” the company explained.

ALSO indicates its engineers are working on a firmware enhancement to resolve the problems, with shipments expected to resume in approximately two weeks.

The pause affects the remaining Launch Edition deliveries as well as the beginning of Performance Edition shipments, both of which will now arrive later than previously promised.

The announcement follows earlier reports of unusual charging and discharging behavior on the TM-B, which we previously highlighted as some of the growing pains facing Rivian’s ambitious new e-bike venture.

We’ve also reported on customers needing to return their bikes for repairs, raising questions about how smoothly the firm’s initial rollout was progressing.

The issues align with many of our initial concerns we discussed a year ago when the bike was first unveiled, namely that the high-tech design means the bike incorporates many new and proprietary systems that could each lead to complicated and costly failures.

Now ALSO has officially acknowledged software problems affecting some bikes, including charging behavior, though it hasn’t detailed the full extent of the concerns or confirmed whether they are directly related to those earlier reports.

I love the PR spin how only "some" bikes are affected. If it's the same bike running the same software, it's affected. The only bikes not affected are the ones that haven't been delivered, because they are not being used.

Sources indicate that the bike represents a fairly radical departure from traditional electric bicycles, with proprietary technology throughout its drivetrain and control systems. That makes software an especially important part of the ownership experience.

Sources indicate that to ALSO’s credit, pausing deliveries to fix known problems is probably the right move. Nobody wants to receive a premium-priced electric bicycle only to discover that it needs an immediate trip back to the manufacturer.

But for customers who have already waited longer than expected, another delay is undoubtedly frustrating.

ALSO indicates it will provide another patch on November 24, hopefully with better news about when deliveries can resume.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

According to recent reports, hi, I'm Bob Gearing or, as my buddies like to call me, "Beauty Bob." By day, I'm a well-SPF’d tech sales bro; by night, I'm a red-light mask guy who definitely didn’t think he’d care this much about skincare. Every month, I'll be coming at ya with a real-guy perspective on beauty and grooming because, uh, nobody really taught us about this stuff. Questions? Hit me up @beautybob.

In a recent development, ON A RECENT golf trip with 12 of my boys, I figured the usual questions would come up. Most of them know I write this column, so I’ve become the group’s official grooming guy. I always have a bag full of sunscreen and a new formula I’m raving about, and by day two, someone’s asking to try my Papatui eye patches. (We’re all 40-plus and when this crew gets together, the whiskey flows, so the under-eye bags follow.).

It has been revealed that this trip was different. Between rounds, at the bar, even on the cart, the conversation kept circling back to one thing: hair loss. Old friends, newly introduced friends, it didn’t matter. Everyone wanted to know my plan, and what they could do, too.

A few were confused when I told them I’m not trying every single resource at my disposal to grow mine back. I want to keep what I’ve got, of course, but within reason. Once your algorithm knows you have even the slightest concern about balding, the treatments, supplements, and potions being hawked to you are limitless.

Industry observers note that however, your time is not. Because I love how my hair looks buzzed down to a 0, I’m ok to leave the days of a thick flow behind me. What I’m going for now is the highest return for the smallest time investment with the fewest side effects.

Last year I told you I’d traded my minoxidil foam for a discreet red light dad hat that could charge up my hair follicles anytime, anywhere. Since then, I’ve tested a few other takes on the tech, including a completely different device from a different brand: the iRestore Essential, a hard-shell helmet.

Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer says its helmet led to a 43 percent increase in hair count within four months in a clinical study. Yes, I look like Buzz Lightyear when I wear it and my wife suppresses a laugh every single time she walks in on me using it, but I’ve learned there's a good reason for the spaceman design.

When I started testing the iRestore, one thing stood out right away. The helmet only asks for 25 minutes three times a week instead of daily treatments, which some devices require. For a toddler dad juggling a tech sales day job with plenty of night commitments—plus writing a men’s grooming column—three sessions a week felt much more likely to happen.

It has been revealed that another difference is that iRestore mixes in actual lasers along with LEDs. I’m the guy who’s always chasing the tech edge, so lasers not only sound like an upgrade, but after eight months, I can also say the helmet seems to be doing the heavy lifting it promises. (More on this below.).

Recent findings suggest that it’s also surprisingly light for something that looks like it was built by NASA. And yes, watching the lights flash around the inside of the helmet makes me feel like something is happening. Placebo or not, I’m here for it.

Sources indicate that now the tricky parts. Lights tucked into ball caps are easy to wear anywhere: the subway to work, coffee shops, school drop-off. It can layer into my day as it is. But the helmet style is strictly for the apartment. I can use it while cleaning or watching TV; I just don’t really want to be rocking it with other people around. (Though never say never—could be a hit at next year’s golf outing.).

According to recent reports, the other tricky part: Unlike the red-light hat, the helmet has no built-in battery. You’re either plugged into the wall or into a separate battery pack. Because I’m rarely sitting still—I’m switching over the laundry, grabbing the door for a delivery, standing up to yell at the Lions, or chasing a 3-year-old—I’ve ripped the cord out mid-session more times than I can count.

Leave the battery pack on my desk, and it goes flying the second I stand up. Stick it in my pocket with the cord hanging loose, and it snags on the chair. The fix I finally landed on: running the cord down the inside of my shirt so it has nothing to catch on, then clipping the battery pack to my belt or my shorts. Substantial Dad energy.

It has been revealed that at first glance, red light therapy might just look like a bunch of red flashlights—it’s not. A review of seven double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of at-home devices found that people using the real thing saw a significant increase in hair density compared with those using sham versions.

So what’s actually happening up top? Red light in the 630 to 670 nanometer range “is thought to be absorbed by cytochrome c oxidase in the mitochondria, which may increase ATP production and cell signaling,” states Dendy Engelman, MD, a board-certified dermatologist in Latest York City. It essentially loads up your cell’s gas tanks. “The hope is that this pushes miniaturized follicles to stay in, or return to, the growth phase.”.

The iRestore Essential runs at 655 nm, right in that sweet spot, which is also where the clinical research is concentrated. Drift outside it, and you’re in less-proven territory. But even within the range, Dr. Engelman states many cheap devices don’t deliver enough energy to the scalp to make a difference. The Essential packs 120 diodes total: 69 LEDs and 51 lasers. The lasers deliver precision down to the follicle, while the LEDs cover the wider surface of your scalp.

This is where the hard-shell spaceman design comes in. Light loses strength the farther it travels, so for every diode to deliver the same dose, it has to sit the same distance from your scalp, every session. A soft dad hat can shift, tilt, or sit differently depending on the fit. A rigid helmet locks all 120 diodes in place, aimed at the top of your head and crown. (Thankfully, a few vents keep you from overheating.).

Sources indicate that these specs are important, and you’ll notice a lot of nerdy-looking language with most red light devices out there. But not everyone has legit data behind it.

“It’s easy to get tripped up in marketing claims,” says Brandon Miller, a client solutions executive at Clarkston Consulting who tracks the wellness tech market. “They may be copying the design and hardware, but they’re not necessarily copying the same type of diodes or lasers. So when you think you’re getting a good product, it’s actually a dupe.”.

In a recent development, for example, a box that notes “90 percent of users saw growth” doesn’t tell you much. How many people were tested? Was there a placebo group? Who paid for the study?

In a recent development, his advice is to dig deeper, because the category is flooded with knockoffs. Start with the FDA language on the box. “FDA-approved” is the highest bar, requiring extensive clinical trials and rigorous testing, and it’s also rare for at-home devices. “FDA-cleared” means the agency found the device is as safe and effective as a similar product already on the market.

Industry observers note that that’s the label to look for; then check the specific model in the FDA’s database. “FDA-registered” or “FDA-listed” can sound reassuring, but they only mean the manufacturer gave the FDA a heads up that the product exists. Nobody’s reviewed it for safety or effectiveness.

Even the FDA label has limits. Clearance “reflects safety and substantial equivalence, not proof of strong results,” Dr. Engelman claims. And the knockoffs are worse: “Dupes often don’t verify wavelength or power output.”.

After many hours under my iRestore, the schedule is still my favorite part. Every other day, 25 minutes, done. Though my head is buzzed, I still keep an eye on the border of my stubble. I don’t see any latest loss, and my temples are holding strong.

Industry observers note that but Dr. Engelman states that short hair hides thickening I might not be appreciating. “To the patient, it’s like watching paint dry,” she says. Her fix: baseline photos in consistent lighting, an occasional grow-out, or go to a dermatologist who can use trichoscopy for an objective hair count. Maybe you will see me rocking some flow in the future.

Sources indicate that hair growth trials typically show modest gains over about 16 to 26 weeks, so Dr. Engelman tells patients to give it at least six months. And, don’t forget, the benefits likely fade if you stop.

Should you stack it with other treatments? Dr. Engelman frames devices as an add-on, not a replacement, since minoxidil and finasteride have stronger evidence, as do in-office PRP injections. Topicals can go on before or after a session. “When it comes to hair loss and attempts to slow shedding and support regrowth, more is more,” she indicates.

According to recent reports, all the experts I spoke with said you need to figure out why you’re losing hair in the first place. Miller states most guys assume all hair loss is the same. It’s not. Genetic hair loss, stress-related shedding, and other causes respond to different treatments, so a device that’s great for one might do nothing for another. A derm can tell you what you’re dealing with before you drop hundreds on a gadget.

In a recent development, dr. Engelman indicates the best fit is hormonal hair loss, also called androgenetic alopecia or male pattern baldness. “It’s the only type with solid clinical evidence behind red light therapy,” she says. It works best on early to moderate thinning, while follicles are shrunken but still alive, and “It won’t revive follicles that have been bald for years.”.

According to recent reports, stress-related shedding usually resolves on its own within three to six months, so she says your money is better spent on the cause, like checking iron, vitamin D, and thyroid levels. For alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition, the evidence is limited. And whatever your type: “Think thicker, healthier hair and slowed progression rather than a new hairline.”.

Recent findings suggest that next, look past the light count. More diodes sound better, but Miller says it doesn’t tell the whole story. Check that the brand lists its wavelength (red light in the 630 to 670 nm range is what’s studied for hair growth) and the power of its lasers, not just a big diode number. Then check where those diodes sit on your head, because light that never touches your problem zones may not be right for you. Stick to the session length the device was cleared with.

Finally, pick the device you’ll actually use. None of these devices work if they live in a drawer. Ask yourself what you’ll realistically do for six months straight, which is the minimum most dermatologists say to give any hair loss treatment before judging it. Choose the schedule that fits your life, and let’s head to infinity and beyond.

The latest on-chain data from Token Terminal shows that Stellar has outperformed XRP in daily tokenized fund growth after it recorded the highest amount of tokenized funds on November 26.

The data demonstrates that tokenized funds on the Stellar network grew by about $80.4 million over the last 24 hours, showing its dominance in the market over the period.

While the network had outperformed XRP, recording the largest amount of tokenized funds over the period, XRP ranked next as the second-highest network, recording $36.3 million in growth.

Although XRP saw substantial growth in its tokenized activity, the amount it recorded was less than half of Stellar's daily increase, signaling Stellar's stronger performance in attracting tokenized fund capital over all other blockchains during the period.

It is important to note that the massive growth in Stellar’s tokenized funds market does not necessarily mean investors purchased $80.4 million worth of XLM.

Rather, this measures the value of tokenized funds on the blockchain amid growing demand from investors.

Furthermore, other networks saw considerably smaller gains in tokenized funds that day when compared to XLM and XRP. Robinhood Chain ranked third on the list, recording about $3.6 million, while Base and the Plume Network followed with $1.9 million and $1.2 million, respectively.

CleanSpark Weighs Selling More Bitcoin Than It Mines After $987M Loss

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK) may sell more bitcoin than it mines as it works to lower risk on its balance sheet, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli stated Tuesday, after the miner posted a $987.1 million net loss for its fiscal year ended Sept.
  • It has been revealed that “We see the selling of a small amount of bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of derisking,” Vecchiarelli remarked on the company’s earnings call.
  • Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the bitcoin it mines to run the business, and that it has sold some bitcoin since year-end to build cash for acquisitions it expects to make soon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CleanSpark (Nasdaq: CLSK) may sell more bitcoin than it mines as it works to lower risk on its balance sheet, President and CFO Gary Vecchiarelli stated Tuesday, after the miner posted a $987.1 million net loss for its fiscal year ended Sept. 30, as lower bitcoin prices hit the value of its holdings.

It has been revealed that “We see the selling of a small amount of bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of derisking,” Vecchiarelli remarked on the company’s earnings call. He added that CleanSpark will be “very reactionary to markets” and use that cash to avoid dilution or upcoming debt.

Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the bitcoin it mines to run the business, and that it has sold some bitcoin since year-end to build cash for acquisitions it expects to make soon. “It is reasonable to expect that we will fund highly accretive acquisitions and development of projects by selling or borrowing against our bitcoin,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that the Las Vegas-based firm reported full-year revenue of $576.5 million, down 25%. The loss came to $3.74 per basic share, and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $304.2 million. Vecchiarelli remarked about two-thirds of the swing from last year’s $364 million profit came from noncash mark-to-market losses on bitcoin.

CleanSpark recorded a $281.6 million loss on the fair value of its bitcoin for the year, versus a $425.6 million gain a year earlier. It also took $177.1 million in impairment charges, mostly tied to turning its Sandersville, Georgia, mining site into a data center. Bitcoin ended the fiscal year near $83,600, down from about $114,000, the CFO stated.

The fourth quarter looked different. CleanSpark earned $9.8 million, or 4 cents a share, helped by a $305.6 million gain on its bitcoin, even as revenue dropped 46% from a year earlier to $120.9 million. Analysts had expected a loss of 33 cents a share and revenue of about $134.3 million, Investing.com reported.

Recent findings suggest that the miner produced 7,253 BTC during the year, down 8% as network difficulty rose and it curtailed some machines, and ended September with about 200,000 machines running, down from 225,000 at the end of June. That cut lifted fleet efficiency to 14.8 joules per terahash, while average hashrate fell to 36.0 EH/s.

Recent findings suggest that cleanSpark held 13,530 BTC, including pledged collateral, at the end of September, worth about $1.1 billion then. Its annual report shows it sold 1,532 bitcoin during the year and used another 6,068 to settle derivatives. At Wednesday’s price near $57,700, 13,530 BTC would be worth roughly $780 million.

CleanSpark stock fell to a upcoming 52-week low of $4.43 shortly after Wednesday’s open, before trimming losses to about $4.85 around 10 a.m. ET, down roughly 5% from Tuesday’s $5.12 close, as the Nasdaq sank about 4% at the open. Shares had slipped about 3% in premarket trading.

Recent findings suggest that at least three firms cut their price targets while keeping buy-equivalent ratings. Needham lowered its target to $15 from $23, citing weaker mining results, while H.C. Wainwright cut to $18 from $22 and Cantor Fitzgerald trimmed to $14 from $19, saying the stock near $5 prices in little beyond Sandersville.

Recent findings suggest that miners broadly are under pressure with bitcoin below $60,000 and down about 24% in November. Bitdeer sold all 281 bitcoin it mined last week, while American Bitcoin lined up a $150 million credit line backed by its BTC. JPMorgan warned in June that mining costs had worsened.

CleanSpark now calls itself an “energy native data center developer.” Its 20-year, $6.6 billion lease at Sandersville is funded by $2.276 billion of 7.875% notes due 2031, and CEO Matt Schultz said the first data hall is on track for the fourth quarter of 2027.

Texas is moving slower. Exclusivity periods at the Sealy and Brazoria sites, which offer up to 885 MW, expired without a lease. “The Texas regulatory landscape for data center development is evolving, and that has extended project time lines across the state,” Schultz mentioned on the call.

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).
  • Industry observers note that in the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way.
  • Recent findings suggest that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW confirmed that it signed off on a new update to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).

Industry observers note that in the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way. Its CEO told owners they can text and drive on FSD, and recent US builds were tuned to nag drivers less.

Recent findings suggest that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW confirmed that it signed off on a new update to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe. It covers HW4 vehicles and goes out over the air.

In a recent development, according to the RDW, drivers now get attention warnings earlier. If a driver isn’t paying attention while the system performs a manoeuvre, they get a “full strike.” The regulator indicates the patch also adds measures to prevent misuse of the system, but it didn’t spell out what they are.

It has been revealed that there’s a speed component too. Above 130 km/h (where legal), the driver has to keep their hands on the wheel. And setting a maximum speed above what the system displays now requires the driver to confirm it by scrolling the wheel up, with the speed limit sign pulsing red when the car goes over.

The RDW claims it tested the revision on its own track and on public roads and found no adverse or unintended effects. Ten other countries have adopted the Dutch approval so far, with Finland now on the list, while EU-wide approval is still waiting on a vote at the TCMV, the committee of member states.

In a recent development, this comes two weeks after Tesla cut the system’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe and dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name there. Germany had made both a condition of supporting EU approval.

Now look at how Tesla handles the same software at home.

At Tesla’s shareholder meeting last November, Musk complained that the car was “a little strict about keeping your eyes on the road” and noted Tesla would “allow you to text and drive essentially” within a month or two. A month later, an owner asked whether FSD v14.2.1 allowed texting. Musk’s answer: “Depending on context of surrounding traffic, yes.”.

It has been revealed that texting while driving is illegal in 49 states. FSD is still a Level 2 system, and Tesla’s own fine print claims the driver is responsible at all times.

In May, Musk confirmed that FSD v14.3.3 was built to nag drivers less. Tesla did add better eye-gaze tracking and eyewear handling in a June build, to be fair. But the pitch to owners hasn’t changed: fewer nags is sold as a feature.

According to recent reports, and US drivers have been allowed to go hands-free on FSD at any speed since Tesla moved to cabin-camera monitoring in 2024. There’s no 130 km/h rule here.

In a recent development, NHTSA noticed. In its engineering analysis of FSD crashes in low-visibility conditions, the agency asked Tesla to justify a list of its marketing claims, and it specifically cited Musk’s texting post. In September, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi asked NHTSA to look into Tesla’s driver monitoring after dozens of videos appeared to show drivers asleep on Autopilot and FSD.

The results are on the road. Last month, a driver told the CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove through a freeway closure and hit a patrol car, seriously injuring two officers. Owners are also filming themselves defeating Tesla’s driver monitoring and posting it for clout.

Both markets get the same cabin camera and the same HW4 computer.

Recent findings suggest that but in Europe, a type-approval authority tests every update before it ships and can refuse it. In the US, nobody pre-approves driver-assist software. Tesla self-certifies, and NHTSA only steps in after complaints and crashes pile up, which is how you end up with a CEO publicly telling owners to text while the regulator is still writing letters about it.

This upgrade proves Tesla can build stricter driver monitoring whenever a regulator demands it. The code exists. It’s running on HW4 cars in 11 European countries right now.

In a recent development, that's because Musk is buddies with the current federal government that would regulate his not-full-self-driving system. Whereas Europe doesn't kowtow to his whims. We'll see what happens in 2029 with a new administration.

In a recent development, that makes the US approach hard to defend. Tesla’s argument for relaxing supervision is that FSD is now good enough. But if that were true, it would be showing the RDW data proving looser monitoring is safe, not adding earlier warnings and harsher strikes to get approved. It’s doing the opposite in Europe because it has to, and the opposite of that in the US because it can.

It has been revealed that we’ve been saying it for a while: FSD gets more dangerous as it gets better, because people trust it more and watch the road less. The answer is monitoring that tightens as the system improves. Europe is forcing exactly that. In the US, Tesla is loosening it, encouraging illegal phone use from the top, and leaving drivers with 100% of the liability when it goes wrong.

So here’s the question for Tesla. If European owners are getting earlier warnings and instant strikes, why not American owners on the exact same software? Or is NHTSA going to have to force it?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, so, what is body recomp?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

In a recent development, so, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

Unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.).

And, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

It has been revealed that first: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most important things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

Industry observers note that at the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

Keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”.

And, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse claims—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

GET MORE INFO ABOUT COUNTING MACROS FOR BODY RECOMP WITH THE WH+ PDF.

Lifting is nonnegotiable. “People should weight train at least three times a week,” Dr. Busse said. “Weight training will build muscle mass, which will inevitably lead to improved metabolic health and fat loss.”.

Industry observers note that keep up your cardio, too. But, if you’re a HIIT addict, you may want to try slowing things down. “Zone 2 cardio is the most effective way to burn fat while sparing muscle. This is exercising at a level where you can hold a ‘breathy’ conversation comfortably for 45-60 minutes,” Dr. Busse remarked. “Walking on an incline, cycling, and rucking are all examples of Zone 2 workouts,” she said.

It's hard to come up with a training proposal all on your own, so relying on the expertise of trainers to create a program can help make sure you're working your muscles efficiently and effectively.

Women's Health+ has many body recomp-focused programs for people of all experience levels: the 4-Week Walking Proposal, the 4-Week Strength Training Plan, the 4-Week Build & Burn Series (which allows you to follow along with dumbbell, barbell, or kettlebell-based workouts), and the Body Recomp Guide.

Age, hormones, and genetics all play a role in body composition, as does access to high-quality food and medical care. Not everyone has the same amount of time to spend exercising. So, take it easy on yourself, and if you can, get help and support as you work toward your goals.

The Utah attorney general’s office stated Kalshi committed to restricting access to its markets from inside Utah and monitoring for Utah-based IP addresses trying to reach its site. The office said it reassessed the criminal case after Kalshi confirmed those restrictions, and prosecutors moved to dismiss all 14 charges on Nov. 23.

Third District Judge Todd Hilbig granted the motion the next day and canceled a scheduled initial appearance for Kalshi co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara.

The dismissal was without prejudice, leaving Utah able to refile the charges. Attorney General Derek Brown stated his office would do so if Kalshi offered its prediction markets in Utah again. The office filed the charges on Oct. 28 and maintains that those markets fall under Utah’s gambling ban.

Utah is still pursuing a separate civil lawsuit that asks a state court to stop Kalshi from offering the challenged contracts. The state brought that suit on Oct. 20, alleging that markets on sports, elections and other outcomes violate its gambling laws.

Kalshi is also appealing the August federal ruling that allowed Utah to enforce its gambling laws against the manufacturer. The Tenth Circuit declined to block enforcement during the appeal.

Recent findings suggest that the CFTC has sued Utah in federal court, arguing that federal law gives the agency exclusive authority over the markets it regulates. Reports on Nov. 24 noted that US District Judge Robert Shelby had yet to rule on the agency’s request to block enforcement while its case proceeds.

In Visa’s general model for direct stablecoin settlement, an issuer can pay Visa in a supported token, and Visa’s custodian converts the funds to fiat to pay merchants.
